examples.why: "est acceptée comme étant" is a word-for-word rendering of the English passive; a French technical writer would use the impersonal "on admet que" / "est communément fixée à".

examples.source: the ability to approximate the energy to this degree comes from prior knowledge about the molecule
examples.suggested: la capacité à estimer l'énergie avec cette précision provient de la connaissance préalable de la molécule
examples.translation: la capacité à approximer l'énergie à ce degré provient de la connaissance préalable de la molécule
examples.why: "à ce degré" is a literal calque of "to this degree"; French uses "avec cette précision" / "à ce niveau de précision". "approximer" is also stiffer than "estimer" here.

examples.source: we will generate a random set of counts for the configuration recovery loop to post-process
examples.suggested: nous allons générer un ensemble aléatoire de comptages que la boucle de récupération de configuration post-traitera
examples.translation: nous allons générer un ensemble aléatoire de comptages pour la boucle de récupération de configuration à post-traiter
examples.why: The trailing "à post-traiter" attaches grammatically to the nearest noun "la boucle", so a reader momentarily parses it as the loop being post-processed rather than the counts; a relative clause removes the ambiguity.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveat (the "ce n'est PAS le temps utilisé pour la facturation (temps QPU)" note, the "sujette à changement" preview warning and the Sampler-only restriction all survive intact), and the informal "tu" register holds everywhere. Three things a native technical editor would still change. (1) `gate` is left in English with a masculine article — "Le gate et le qubit sur lequel opérer" and "le gate X appliqué au qubit 10" — where French Qiskit prose says "la porte (quantique)"; recognizable, but an anglicism no French quantum writer would produce, and the masculine gender compounds it. (2) "scheduling" is rendered two ways in the same file: "1 cycle de planification" (twice) vs "dans l'ordonnancement complet" and "le timing de l'ordonnancement du circuit" — pick one. (3) Residual stiffness/calque: "Elle est en statut de version préliminaire" for "It is in preview release status" (natural French: "Elle est en version préliminaire"), plus an incongruous capital in "la valeur `dt` d'un Backend" (twice) where every other occurrence of the term is lowercase.

examples.source: `Instruction` - The gate and the qubit to operate on. … a control pulse for the X gate applied to qubit 10
examples.suggested: La porte et le qubit sur lequel opérer. … une impulsion de contrôle pour la porte X appliquée au qubit 10
examples.translation: `Instruction` - Le gate et le qubit sur lequel opérer. … une impulsion de contrôle pour le gate X appliqué au qubit 10
examples.why: French quantum documentation uses "porte (quantique)" for gate; the untranslated "le gate" is an anglicism, and the masculine article makes it read as raw MT. Consistent and recognizable, so not misleading — but a native editor would change every occurrence.

examples.source: T0 - The instruction start time within the complete schedule … 1 dt = 1 scheduling cycle … Next, get the circuit schedule timing
examples.suggested: Use one rendering of schedule/scheduling — e.g. "ordonnancement" throughout: "1 dt = 1 cycle d'ordonnancement"
examples.translation: L'instant de début de l'instruction dans l'ordonnancement complet … 1 dt = 1 cycle de planification … Ensuite, obtiens le timing de l'ordonnancement du circuit
examples.why: The same underlying concept (the scheduler's cycle vs the schedule the instruction sits in) is split between "planification" and "ordonnancement" within a few lines, obscuring that both refer to the one `scheduler_timing` schedule.

examples.source: It is in preview release status and is therefore subject to change.
examples.suggested: Elle est en version préliminaire et peut donc évoluer.
examples.translation: Elle est en statut de version préliminaire et est donc sujette à changement.
examples.why: "en statut de version préliminaire" is a word-for-word calque of "in preview release status"; French drops the "statut de" scaffolding. Grammatical but stiff.

examples.source: You can find the `dt` value of a backend by using `backend.dt`.
examples.suggested: …la valeur `dt` d'un backend en utilisant…
examples.translation: Tu peux trouver la valeur `dt` d'un Backend en utilisant [`backend.dt`]
examples.why: Stray capital on "Backend" in both occurrences, inconsistent with the lowercase common-noun use elsewhere in the corpus; reads as an untidied term-substitution artifact.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, no invented claims — and the keep-English strategy for `pass manager` / `transpiler pass` / `backend` / `StagedPassManager` is the right call for this field. Two things a native technical editor would fix: (1) "pass manager(s)" is rendered three ways in one file — Hebrew "מנהלי מעברים" in the title/sidebar_label/description, English "pass manager" in every body paragraph, and Hebrew again in one stray body line ("בשימוש במנהלי מעברים רבים", line 183); pick one and make the body match the title. (2) A real noun error: "כל הרצפות הרצופות של שערים חד-Qubit" (line 36) uses רְצָפוֹת = "floors/tiles"; the plural of רֶצֶף (sequence) is רְצָפִים, so it should be "כל הרצפים הרצופים". Smaller: a missing maqaf in "בעוד שpass manager רגיל" (line 40), the over-formal "למכשיר המטרה הנקוב" for "the specified target device" (line 185, natural Hebrew is "שצוין"), and the hybrid "חד-Qubit"/"דו-Qubit" with a capitalized English noun glued to a Hebrew prefix (lines 36, 64, 91, 111).

examples.source: Transpile with pass managers / …used in many pass managers.
examples.suggested: Keep the English term in the body as the file already does, and use it in line 183 too: "…שנמצאת בשימוש ב-pass managers רבים" — or Hebraize consistently everywhere including the body.
examples.translation: טרנספילציה עם מנהלי מעברים (title/description) … staged pass manager / pass manager (all body paragraphs) … "פונקציונליות נפוצה שנמצאת בשימוש במנהלי מעברים רבים" (line 183)
examples.why: The same core object of the page is named in Hebrew in the title and sidebar, in English in every explanatory paragraph, and in Hebrew again in one isolated sentence. A reader scanning the page sees two names for one concept; within-file inconsistency, not misleading.

examples.source: one pass could go through the circuit and merge all consecutive sequences of single-qubit gates
examples.suggested: …ולמזג את כל הרצפים הרצופים של שערים חד-קיוביטיים
examples.translation: pass אחד יכול לעבור על המעגל ולמזג את כל הרצפות הרצופות של שערים חד-Qubit
examples.why: רְצָפוֹת is the plural of רִצְפָּה (floor/tiling), not of רֶצֶף (sequence) — the correct plural is רְצָפִים. Context keeps the meaning recoverable, but it reads as a wrong-word slip no native technical writer would leave.

examples.source: While a normal pass manager is composed of several transpiler passes…
examples.suggested: בעוד ש-pass manager רגיל מורכב ממספר transpiler passes
examples.translation: בעוד שpass manager רגיל מורכב ממספר transpiler passes
examples.why: Missing maqaf between the Hebrew prefix ש and the Latin-script term. The rest of the file does this correctly ("ב-Qiskit", "מ-`qiskit_ibm_runtime`"), so it is an isolated typography lapse in RTL/LTR mixing.

examples.source: …to "embed" a selected initial `Layout` from a layout pass to the specified target device.
examples.suggested: …למכשיר המטרה שצוין.
examples.translation: ל-"הטמעת" `Layout` ראשוני שנבחר מ-layout pass למכשיר המטרה הנקוב.
examples.why: הנקוב is elevated/administrative Hebrew ("the stated/nominal"), out of step with the informal instructional register the rest of the page keeps ("בואו נעשה זאת", "אין הגבלה… שאפשר לשים"). שצוין is the ordinary technical word for "specified".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped values or dropped caveats (approximation_degree 1.0/0.0, the sabre/translator/alap defaults, and the "initial_layout overrides the passes" caveat all survive intact), and the informal imperative register ("צור מעגל וצפה בתוצאה", "אם תציין") holds. The main defect is terminology: "unitary synthesis" is rendered four times as "סינתזת היחידה" ("synthesis of the unit/identity" — "מטריצת היחידה" is precisely the Hebrew for the identity matrix); the correct term is "סינתזה אוניטרית". Secondly, "unroll" in `basis_gates` is rendered "פריסה", the same word the file uses throughout for "layout" ("שלב פריסה", "פריסה התחלתית", "פרמטרי פריסה וטופולוגיה"), so under a layout-titled accordion the basis-gate entry reads as if it were about layout; "פירוק" would keep the two apart. Smaller items: the "heuristic dial" metaphor breaks as "חיוג היוריסטי" (phone-dialing, not a knob — "חוגה"), "ground state" is "מצב הבסיסי" instead of the physics-standard "מצב היסוד", the ungrammatical form "ולא בוצעת שום התאמה" (should be "ולא מתבצעת"), and calqued phrasing such as "מפת צימוד מכוונת (אפשרי מותאמת אישית) ליעד במיפוי" and "פותח בשימוש בדרישות הבאות".

examples.source: The name of the unitary synthesis method to use. ... an optional configuration dictionary that is passed directly to the unitary synthesis plugin
examples.suggested: שם שיטת הסינתזה האוניטרית (unitary synthesis) לשימוש. ... לפלאגין הסינתזה האוניטרית
examples.translation: שם שיטת סינתזת היחידה לשימוש. ... מילון תצורה אופציונלי שמועבר ישירות לפלאגין סינתזת היחידה
examples.why: 'unitary' is 'אוניטרי' in Hebrew physics/math; 'יחידה' is unit/identity ('מטריצת היחידה' = identity matrix), so the reader is pointed at a different object. Used consistently but consistently wrong, 4 occurrences.

examples.source: List of basis gate names to unroll to. For example ['u1','u2','u3','cx']. If None, do not unroll.
examples.suggested: רשימת שמות שערי בסיס לפירוק אליהם (unroll). ... אם None, אל תבצע פירוק.
examples.translation: רשימת שמות שערי בסיס לפריסה אליהם. לדוגמה ['u1','u2','u3','cx']. אם None, אל תבצע פריסה.
examples.why: 'פריסה' is already this file's word for 'layout' (שלב פריסה / פריסה התחלתית / פרמטרי פריסה וטופולוגיה), and this bullet sits inside the layout accordion — the collision makes basis_gates read as a layout option.

examples.source: Heuristic dial used for circuit approximation (1.0 = no approximation, 0.0 = maximal approximation).
examples.suggested: חוגה היוריסטית לכוונון קירוב המעגל (1.0 = ללא קירוב, 0.0 = קירוב מקסימלי).
examples.translation: חיוג היוריסטי המשמש לקירוב מעגל (1.0 = ללא קירוב, 0.0 = קירוב מקסימלי).
examples.why: 'חיוג' is dialing a phone number, not a control knob; the 'turn the dial between two extremes' intuition the English gives the learner is lost.

examples.source: Schedule instructions late, that is, keeping qubits in the ground state when possible (alias: alap).
examples.suggested: תזמן הוראות מאוחר ככל האפשר, כלומר, השאר qubit-ים במצב היסוד כשניתן (כינוי: alap).
examples.translation: תזמן הוראות מאוחר, כלומר, שמור qubit-ים במצב הבסיסי כאשר אפשרי (כינוי: alap).
examples.why: Ground state is 'מצב היסוד' in Hebrew physics; 'מצב הבסיסי' reads as 'the basic state' and risks being taken for a basis state (מצב בסיס).

examples.source: If the QPU doesn't have any restriction on the instruction time allocation, timing_constraints is None and no adjustment is performed. / Directed coupling map (possibly custom) to target in mapping.
examples.suggested: `timing_constraints` הוא `None` ולא מתבצעת שום התאמה. / מפת צימוד מכוונת (אפשר מותאמת אישית) שאליה יש למפות.
examples.translation: `timing_constraints` הוא `None` ולא בוצעת שום התאמה. / מפת צימוד מכוונת (אפשרי מותאמת אישית) ליעד במיפוי.
examples.why: 'בוצעת' is a wrong verb form (2nd-person feminine past) where present-passive is needed; 'אפשרי מותאמת אישית' is ungrammatical and 'ליעד במיפוי' is a word-for-word calque of 'to target in mapping' that does not parse as Hebrew.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads — quantities, caveats and claims are faithful (row 15/column 20, $N(N+1)/2$ unique entries, "eksak (hingga shot noise)", optimization_level=3, the seven-qubit instance reused on hardware), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. But a native technical editor would change several things. (1) "circuit" is rendered two ways within the file: "sirkuit" in the Background/Step-1 prose ("sirkuit kuantum", "sirkuit kernel kuantum", "gate terparameter pada sirkuit") but left as English "circuit" from Step 1 onward ("Circuit abstrak", "circuit overlap", "circuit ditranspilasi") — pick one. (2) "classical" is consistently rendered "klasikal" ("input klasikal", "analog klasikal", "Secara klasikal", "format klasikal"); in Indonesian "klasikal" means "classroom-based" — the physics/computing term is "klasik". (3) Recurring translationese: inanimate "mereka" for English "they/their" ("bagaimana mereka dapat menyediakan ruang fitur", "mengapa mereka penting", "perkalian dalam mereka"), plus calqued syntax in the hardware-example paragraph ("setiap entri memerlukan menjalankan circuit overlap", "kita oleh karena itu menjalankan") and "Jika kamu menemukan karya ini menarik". (4) "the feature-mapped space" becomes "ruang yang telah dipetakan oleh fitur" (space mapped *by* features), which quietly inverts the agency of the feature map.

examples.source: Output: Abstract circuit for calculating a kernel matrix entry. / We create the quantum circuit used to evaluate one entry in the kernel matrix.
examples.suggested: Use one rendering file-wide — either "sirkuit" everywhere ("Sirkuit abstrak", "sirkuit overlap", "sirkuit ditranspilasi") or English "circuit" everywhere.
examples.translation: Output: Circuit abstrak untuk menghitung entri matriks kernel. / Kita membuat sirkuit kuantum yang digunakan untuk mengevaluasi satu entri dalam matriks kernel.
examples.why: Within-file term split: the Background and Step-1 prose say "sirkuit", every later step says "circuit". Recognizable either way, but a reader sees the same object named two ways in adjacent paragraphs.

examples.source: effectively replacing classical analogs / Classically, feature maps of interest… / Map classical inputs to a quantum problem / return result in desired classical format
examples.suggested: analog klasik / Secara klasik / input klasik / format klasik
examples.translation: secara efektif menggantikan analog klasikal / Secara klasikal, peta fitur yang menarik… / Petakan input klasikal ke masalah kuantum / kembalikan hasil dalam format klasikal yang diinginkan
examples.why: In Indonesian, "klasikal" means classroom-based/collective (KBBI: bersangkutan dengan kelas); the established term for classical physics/computing is "klasik" (komputasi klasik, fisika klasik). Consistent but an imperfect, faintly false-friend choice.

examples.source: …and each entry requires running an overlap circuit whose two-qubit-gate depth grows with the size of the feature map… To keep the demo short and to make a clean comparison, we therefore run the same seven-qubit instance…
examples.suggested: …dan setiap entri mengharuskan kita menjalankan sirkuit overlap yang kedalaman gate dua-qubitnya tumbuh seiring ukuran peta fitur… Karena itu, agar demo tetap singkat dan perbandingannya bersih, kita menjalankan instans tujuh-qubit yang sama…
examples.translation: …dan setiap entri memerlukan menjalankan circuit overlap yang kedalaman gate dua-qubitnya bertumbuh seiring ukuran peta fitur… Agar demo tetap singkat dan perbandingan bersih, kita oleh karena itu menjalankan instans tujuh-qubit yang sama…
examples.why: "memerlukan menjalankan" is not idiomatic (memerlukan takes a noun, not a bare verb), and "kita oleh karena itu menjalankan" transplants English adverb placement; a native writer fronts "Karena itu".

examples.source: Quantum kernels and how they can provide enhanced feature spaces / why they are important / returns their inner product
examples.suggested: Kernel kuantum dan bagaimana kernel tersebut dapat menyediakan ruang fitur yang ditingkatkan / mengapa hal itu penting / mengembalikan hasil kali dalam keduanya
examples.translation: Kernel kuantum dan bagaimana mereka dapat menyediakan ruang fitur yang ditingkatkan / mengapa mereka penting / mengembalikan perkalian dalam mereka
examples.why: "mereka" is reserved for people in Indonesian; using it for kernels and vectors is a direct English-pronoun calque. "hasil kali dalam" is also the standard mathematical term for inner product over "perkalian dalam".

examples.source: Taking the vectors in the feature-mapped space as arguments… when the inner product in the feature-mapped space can be written in terms of the original data vectors
examples.suggested: …vektor-vektor dalam ruang hasil pemetaan fitur… / ketika hasil kali dalam di ruang fitur hasil pemetaan…
examples.translation: Mengambil vektor-vektor dalam ruang yang telah dipetakan oleh fitur sebagai argumen… ketika perkalian dalam di ruang yang dipetakan fitur dapat ditulis dalam bentuk vektor data asli
examples.why: "dipetakan oleh fitur" reads as "mapped by the features", inverting who maps what: the feature map sends data into feature space. The equation rescues the reader, so it is a nuance loss rather than a false statement.

editor_note: Content is faithful and no passage would teach a false concept; core terms are correct and consistent (matriks Pauli, produk tensor, nilai eigen/vektor eigen, dekomposisi spektral, pengukuran proyektif, observabel, bobot, estimasi fase), and the informal "kita/kamu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change is translationese: "Dengan kata-kata" for "In words" (should be "Dengan kata lain"), "Pertimbangkan pertama matriks Hermitian sembarang A" (English word order; native = "Pertama, pertimbangkan…"), "bersikeras" for "insist", "keakraban dengan dasar-dasar teori grup" for "familiarity with", and repeated animate "mereka" for matrices ("Tetapi mereka juga merupakan matriks Hermitian", "di mana mereka muncul"). Two small meaning slips: the weight definition reads garbled as "jumlah qubit yang menjadi aksinya secara non-trivial" (English: the qubits it acts on non-trivially), and the manner clause "as these measurements are described here" became causal "karena pengukuran-pengukuran ini dijelaskan di sini". Also, the second "finitely many" is dropped ("hanya akan ada sejumlah hasil pengukuran yang berbeda" vs "finitely many different measurement outcomes"), and matrix rank is rendered "peringkat" rather than the more usual "rank" — recognizable, but worth normalizing. Note the file keeps "circuit" and "gate" in English consistently, which is a defensible convention and not counted as a defect.

examples.source: Intuitively speaking, the weight of an $n$-qubit Pauli operation is the number of qubits on which it acts non-trivially.
examples.suggested: Secara intuitif, bobot operasi Pauli $n$-qubit adalah banyaknya qubit yang dikenai aksinya secara non-trivial.
examples.translation: Secara intuitif, bobot dari operasi Pauli $n$-qubit adalah jumlah qubit yang menjadi aksinya secara non-trivial.
examples.why: "yang menjadi aksinya" is a garbled calque of "on which it acts" — literally "that become its action". The intended relation (qubits acted upon) survives only because the preceding sentence already defined weight; a native writer would use "yang dikenai"/"tempat operasi itu bekerja".

examples.source: but, as these measurements are described here, we're taking the eigenvalues $+1$ and $-1$ to be the actual measurement outcomes.
examples.suggested: tetapi, sebagaimana pengukuran-pengukuran ini dijelaskan di sini, kita mengambil nilai eigen $+1$ dan $-1$ sebagai hasil pengukuran yang sebenarnya.
examples.translation: tetapi, karena pengukuran-pengukuran ini dijelaskan di sini, kita mengambil nilai eigen $+1$ dan $-1$ sebagai hasil pengukuran yang sebenarnya.
examples.why: English "as … are described here" is manner ("in the way described here"), not cause. "karena" turns it into a causal claim, which is a small logical shift rather than the intended "under the description used here".

examples.source: but because matrices have only finitely many eigenvalues, there will only be finitely many different measurement outcomes for a given choice of $A$.
examples.suggested: … hanya akan ada sejumlah terbatas hasil pengukuran yang berbeda untuk pilihan $A$ yang diberikan.
examples.translation: tetapi karena matriks hanya memiliki sejumlah terbatas nilai eigen, hanya akan ada sejumlah hasil pengukuran yang berbeda untuk pilihan $A$ yang diberikan.
examples.why: The second "finitely many" loses its qualifier: "sejumlah hasil pengukuran yang berbeda" just means "a number of different outcomes". The parallel with the first clause rescues the sense, but the finiteness — the whole point of the sentence — is no longer stated.

examples.source: Consider first an arbitrary Hermitian matrix $A.$ … In words, the possible outcomes are … if we insist that the eigenvalues are ordered in decreasing value
examples.suggested: Pertama, tinjau matriks Hermitian sembarang $A.$ … Dengan kata lain, hasil yang mungkin adalah … jika kita mensyaratkan nilai eigen diurutkan secara menurun
examples.translation: Pertimbangkan pertama matriks Hermitian sembarang $A.$ … Dengan kata-kata, kemungkinan hasil adalah … jika kita bersikeras bahwa nilai eigen diurutkan dalam nilai yang menurun
examples.why: Three consecutive calques: fronted "Pertimbangkan pertama" copies English word order; "Dengan kata-kata" is a word-for-word "In words" that Indonesian does not use; "bersikeras" is the emotional sense of "insist" rather than the mathematical "require/impose".

examples.source: But they're also Hermitian matrices … where they arose in the context of quantum state tomography.
examples.suggested: Tetapi matriks-matriks ini juga bersifat Hermitian … yang muncul dalam konteks tomografi keadaan kuantum.
examples.translation: Tetapi mereka juga merupakan matriks *Hermitian* … di mana mereka muncul dalam konteks tomografi keadaan kuantum.
examples.why: "mereka" is the animate third-person plural; Indonesian technical prose does not use it for matrices or measurements. Combined with "di mana" as a relative pronoun (another English calque), the passage reads as translated rather than written.

examples.source: The two corresponding projections will therefore have rank higher than one … will both have rank $2^{n-1}.$
examples.suggested: … akan memiliki rank lebih dari satu … keduanya akan memiliki rank $2^{n-1}.$
examples.translation: Dua proyeksi yang bersesuaian karenanya akan memiliki peringkat yang lebih tinggi dari satu … keduanya akan memiliki peringkat $2^{n-1}.$
examples.why: "peringkat" primarily means ranking/position in Indonesian; Indonesian linear-algebra texts normally keep "rank" for matrix rank. It stays recognizable in context, so this is an imperfect-but-understandable rendering rather than a misleading one.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim, condition and caveat matches the English (parameter values required for parametrized circuits, Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs, the experimental-feature warning on fractional gates), and the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("puoi", "devi", "Segui", "Usa", "consulta"). The defect is a glossary leak in the opening paragraph, where "circuit" is left as English capitalized "Circuit" three times ("uno o più Circuit quantistici", "I Circuit dinamici", "se vengono inviati Circuit parametrizzati") while the very same sentence — and the rest of the file (lines 71, 73, 85, 111) — correctly uses "circuito/circuiti"; the split is inside one sentence, which reads as an unfinished machine pass rather than a deliberate keep-in-English convention. Secondary: "Usa il Transpiler per farlo" (line 85) capitalizes the tool name where the English has the common noun "the transpiler", and the same concept appears three ways across the file ("il Transpiler", "la transpilazione", the section label "Transpila"); "il decoupling dinamico" (line 15) is a half-calque where Italian practice keeps "dynamical decoupling" whole, next to the correctly untranslated "twirling". The note title ":::note[gate frazionari]" is also lowercased against the English "Fractional gates" and against every other title in the file.

examples.source: The Sampler's core task is sampling the output register from the execution of one or more quantum circuits. Dynamic circuits and parameterized circuits are accepted as input (if parametrized circuits are submitted, ...)
examples.suggested: ... di uno o più circuiti quantistici. I [circuiti dinamici] e i circuiti parametrizzati sono accettati come input (se vengono inviati circuiti parametrizzati, ...)
examples.translation: Il compito principale di Sampler è campionare il registro di output dall'esecuzione di uno o più Circuit quantistici. I [Circuit dinamici] e i circuiti parametrizzati sono accettati come input (se vengono inviati Circuit parametrizzati, ...)
examples.why: Untranslated capitalized "Circuit" three times, contradicted by "i circuiti parametrizzati" in the same sentence and by "circuito" everywhere else in the file — an unfinished glossary leak, not a keep-in-English convention.

examples.source: Use the transpiler to do this.
examples.suggested: Usa il transpiler per farlo.
examples.translation: Usa il Transpiler per farlo.
examples.why: English has the common noun, not a product name; the file then renders the same concept three ways ("il Transpiler", "la transpilazione" line 148, "Transpila" as a section label) instead of settling on one.

examples.source: Sampler also supports built-in dynamical decoupling and twirling for error suppression.
examples.suggested: Sampler supporta anche il dynamical decoupling integrato e il twirling per la soppressione degli errori.
examples.translation: Sampler supporta anche il decoupling dinamico integrato e il twirling per la soppressione degli errori.
examples.why: Half-calque: Italian technical writing keeps "dynamical decoupling" as a unit (as the sentence itself does for "twirling"); splitting it into "decoupling dinamico" reads as machine output.

examples.source: :::note[Fractional gates]
examples.suggested: :::note[Gate frazionari]
examples.translation: :::note[gate frazionari]
examples.why: Lowercased admonition title, inconsistent with every other heading and title in the file ("Versioni dei pacchetti", "Raccomandazioni") and with the English.

editor_note: Strong, genuinely native-sounding IBM Cloud IAM guide: the tu register is held throughout ("Quando crei un'istanza", "fai clic su", "consulta questa tabella"), the UI-step sequences and the two comparison tables are rendered faithfully, and the conditional in the "Risorse" note ("se stessi creando una policy da applicare solo a una determinata istanza, sceglieresti invece...") correctly preserves the English counterfactual. The single thing a native technical editor would change is the half-translated Qiskit Runtime primitive pair in the actions table: `quantum-computing.session.create` is described as "Crea una Sessione/Batch", translating Session but leaving Batch in English, where both are API object names and the Italian convention is to keep the pair intact ("Crea una Session/Batch"). Nothing here misleads: no inverted conditions, no swapped role/permission cells, no dropped caveats — the Manager/Writer/Reader role columns and the "Solo su una particolare istanza" qualifiers all match the source. Borderline-but-defensible choices I did not count: the impersonal "si raccomanda di creare" for "it's recommended that you create", "Piano Premium" for "Premium Plan", and "Dipende da una condizione" as the legend gloss for "Involves a dependency".

examples.source: | `quantum-computing.session.create` | Create a Session/Batch | Manager, Writer |
examples.suggested: Crea una Session/Batch
examples.translation: | `quantum-computing.session.create` | Crea una Sessione/Batch | Manager, Writer |
examples.why: Session and Batch are both qiskit-ibm-runtime object names; translating only the first half of the pair splits a single API concept and reads as inconsistent to an Italian quantum developer, who keeps both in English.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, the physics passages (縮約純粋度 range [0.5,1], q-sphere latitudes/ハミング距離, RCCX "相対位相まで一致した…アンコンピュート") all track the English, and register is consistent polite desu/masu with no keigo. What a native editor would fix is a set of untranslated/garbled leftovers and a clear two-pass-merge terminology split. Leftovers: 「単一QubitをState は次のように表せます」(L347) is ungrammatical with "State" left in English; 「任意の単一QubitゲートのConstrucを可能にします」(L689) contains the truncated English fragment "Construc"; 「あなたのシーキット」(L307) is a nonsense katakana transliteration of "circuit" used nowhere else in the file; "Terminus/terminus" (L339, L355, L437) is left untranslated instead of 末端/終端; 「Transpilerされた Circuit」(L325) should be トランスパイルされた; 「Qubits を操作する」(L443) keeps the English plural -s; and L327 runs two sentences together with no break (「…ダウンロードできますOpenQASMのCircuitは…」). Terminology splits across the file halves: Gate vs ゲート, オペレーション vs 操作, Circuit vs 量子回路 vs シーキット, フェーズ vs 位相, ブロッホ球 (L377/L424) vs Bloch球 (L561/L647), ターゲット (L153) vs 標的 (L469), コントロール修飾子 (L149) vs 制御修飾子 (L587) for the same UI element. One small drift: L143 says 「レジスターの数を増減」 where the English says you change the number of qubits or bits (not of registers), and L32 drops the English's "on quantum processing units (QPUs)", losing the first introduction of the QPU abbreviation.

examples.source: A single-qubit state can be represented as
examples.suggested: 単一Qubitの状態は次のように表せます
examples.translation: 単一QubitをStateは次のように表せます
examples.why: Ungrammatical particle (を where の状態は is needed) plus an untranslated English word "State" left mid-sentence; no native writer would produce this line.

examples.source: The three parameters allow the construction of any single-qubit gate.
examples.suggested: 3つのパラメータにより、任意の単一Qubitゲートを構成できます。
examples.translation: 3つのパラメータにより、任意の単一QubitゲートのConstrucを可能にします。
examples.why: "Construc" is a truncated English fragment left in the prose — an obvious untranslated leftover, and the ～のConstrucを可能にします construction is broken Japanese.

examples.source: Next, you can set the number of shots (executions) of your circuit that the backend will perform.
examples.suggested: 次に、BackendがCircuitを実行するショット数（実行回数）を設定できます。
examples.translation: 次に、Backendがあなたのシーキットを実行するショット数（実行回数）を設定できます。
examples.why: 「シーキット」 is a garbled katakana transliteration of "circuit" that appears nowhere else (the file uses Circuit/量子回路), and 「あなたの」 is a calque of possessive "your" that Japanese technical prose drops.

examples.source: except the phase disk, which appears at the end of each qubit wire
examples.suggested: フェーズディスクは各Qubitワイヤーの末端に表示されます
examples.translation: フェーズディスクは各QubitワイヤーのTerminusに表示されます
examples.why: "Terminus" is left in English here and at L355, and lowercase "terminus" at L437 — an ordinary English word, not a domain term the field keeps untranslated.

examples.source: You can increase or decrease the number of qubits or bits in your circuit and rename the registers.
examples.suggested: Circuit内のQubitやビットの数を増減したり、レジスター名を変更したりできます。
examples.translation: Circuitのレジスターの数を増減したり、レジスター名を変更したりできます。
examples.why: The English lets you change the number of qubits/bits inside the registers; the Japanese says you change the number of registers — a different operation, though the following sentence keeps the reader oriented.

examples.source: control modifier / target
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering per term across the file (e.g. 制御修飾子 / 標的).
examples.translation: コントロール修飾子・ターゲット (L149–153) vs 制御修飾子・標的 (L587, L469)
examples.why: Classic two-pass-merge split: the same UI element and the same role are named two different ways in the walkthrough half and the glossary half, alongside Gate/ゲート, オペレーション/操作, フェーズ/位相, ブロッホ球/Bloch球.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no dropped caveats, and the hard terms land correctly (decoherence→결어긋남, encode→부호화, break-even point→손익분기점, logical/physical qubit→논리/물리 Qubit). The defects are consistency and polish. Casing of the kept-English terms is split within the file: "qubit 자체도" (lowercase) vs "해당 Qubit에", "$5$-qubit 코드" vs "9-Qubit Shor 코드", and "Quantum Circuit" vs bare "Circuit" for the same English "circuit"; "labelled" is likewise rendered two ways ("라벨이 붙은" §65, "라벨링된" §69). One imprecision: "at a high enough rate" becomes "충분히 높은 비율로 제거" (§69), where 비율 reads as proportion rather than the intended speed/rate — 속도 is the right word since the point is keeping pace with entropy buildup. Finally a few calqued openers ("가설적으로 말하자면" for "Hypothetically speaking", "확률을 연관시킬 수 있는" §35) and the sentence at §71 keep English word order in a way a Korean technical writer would restructure; the whole file is 합니다체 rather than the 해요체 house register, which is defensible for docs but worth noting.

examples.source: the qubits themselves will be susceptible to noise … the 9-qubit Shor code
examples.suggested: Pick one casing for the kept-English term and apply it everywhere (e.g. always "qubit", or always "Qubit"); likewise use one form for circuit rather than alternating "Quantum Circuit" and bare "Circuit".
examples.translation: qubit 자체도 … / 저장된 각 Qubit에는 … / $5$-qubit 코드 … / 9-Qubit Shor 코드
examples.why: The same term appears in three surface forms inside one short lesson; the concept stays identifiable, so this is polish, not a misleading defect.

examples.source: constant work is required to remove it from the system at a high enough rate
examples.suggested: 시스템에서 엔트로피를 충분히 빠른 속도로 제거하기 위한 지속적인 작업이 필요합니다
examples.translation: 시스템에서 그것을 충분히 높은 비율로 제거하기 위한 지속적인 작업이 필요합니다
examples.why: "rate" here is a speed (entropy removal must outpace its buildup); 비율 reads as a proportion/fraction, blurring the pedagogical point about parallel, frequent EC rounds.

examples.source: we require a precise mathematical model — a noise model — through which probabilities for various things to go wrong can be associated. Hypothetically speaking, …
examples.suggested: 여러 가지 오류가 발생할 *확률*을 부여할 수 있는 정확한 수학적 모델 … 원칙적으로는,
examples.translation: 여러 가지 일이 잘못될 *확률*을 연관시킬 수 있는 정확한 수학적 모델 … 가설적으로 말하자면,
examples.why: "확률을 연관시키다" is a word-for-word calque of "associate probabilities" (Korean would say 확률을 부여하다/할당하다), and "가설적으로 말하자면" is a literal rendering of "Hypothetically speaking" that no native technical writer would open with.

examples.source: There are therefore specific choices that must be made, including the selection of the gadgets as well as the quantum error correcting code itself.
examples.suggested: 따라서 어떤 가젯을 쓸지, 그리고 어떤 양자 오류 정정 코드를 쓸지 등 구체적으로 결정해야 할 사항들이 있습니다.
examples.translation: 따라서 가젯의 선택뿐만 아니라 양자 오류 정정 코드 자체의 선택을 포함하여 이루어져야 하는 특정한 선택들이 있습니다.
examples.why: The English "there are … choices that must be made, including …" frame is carried over intact, producing a nested 선택…선택들 construction that is grammatical but stiff and repetitive in Korean.

examples.source: Perhaps more likely, there could be errors that are localized but that nevertheless affect multiple components in a quantum computer.
examples.suggested: 어쩌면 그보다 더 있을 법한 경우는, 국소적이면서도 …
examples.translation: 더 가능성이 높은 경우는, 국소적이면서도 양자 컴퓨터의 여러 구성 요소에 영향을 주는 오류가 존재하는 상황입니다.
examples.why: The hedge "Perhaps" is dropped, turning a speculative comparison into a flat assertion that this case is more likely; the claim is mildly strengthened but the surrounding argument still reads correctly.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift found: the appendix condition (기하학적 분리 ≈ √N, 고전 복잡도 ~N vs 양자 투영 복잡도 ≪ N), the 80-minute QPU caveat, and the toxic/non-toxic labeling setup all match the English exactly, and core terms (관측량, 기댓값, 축약 밀도 행렬, 특성 맵, 서포트 벡터 머신) are correct. The defect is within-file terminology inconsistency: the Background section writes 큐비트 and 양자 회로 in Korean, but from "Step 3" onward the same concepts appear as raw English glossary leaks mid-sentence — "모든 Qubit에 대한 … 단일 qubit 측정" (three casings of qubit in one line 406), "양자 Circuit을 실행하고" (417), "Circuit 크기와 2-Qubit Gate 깊이" (557), "사용할 Backend를 선택합니다" (407), and the heading "### 양자 Circuit" (330). Separately, "near-term hardware" is rendered as the stiff calque "근시일 내(near-term) 양자 하드웨어" / "근시일 내 장치" (38), which no Korean quantum writer would use (단기/근미래 is conventional), and the Next-steps admonition slips into honorific "흥미로우셨다면 … 살펴보시기 바랍니다" (1037) against the file's otherwise plain 합니다체.

examples.source: The 1-RDMs are a collection of single-qubit measurements of Pauli ``X``, ``Y`` and ``Z`` operators on all qubits. This is because a single-qubit RDM can be fully expressed as:
examples.suggested: 1-RDM은 모든 큐비트에 대한 파울리 ``X``, ``Y``, ``Z`` 연산자의 단일 큐비트 측정 모음입니다. 단일 큐비트 RDM은 다음과 같이 완전히 표현될 수 있기 때문입니다:
examples.translation: 1-RDM은 모든 Qubit에 대한 파울리 ``X``, ``Y``, ``Z`` 연산자의 단일 qubit 측정 모음입니다. 단일 qubit RDM은 다음과 같이 완전히 표현될 수 있기 때문입니다:
examples.why: The Background section (lines 36, 38) already established 큐비트; here the same term appears three ways in one sentence (Qubit / qubit / qubit) as an untranslated glossary leak. Inconsistent, and the capitalized 'Qubit' mid-sentence is not Korean orthography.

examples.source: We print out the circuit size and the two-qubit gate depth. / First we select the backend to use. / Then we run the quantum circuit and measure the projections.
examples.suggested: 회로 크기와 2큐비트 게이트 깊이를 출력합니다. / 먼저 사용할 백엔드를 선택합니다. / 그런 다음 양자 회로를 실행하고 투영값을 측정합니다.
examples.translation: Circuit 크기와 2-Qubit Gate 깊이를 출력합니다. / 먼저 사용할 Backend를 선택합니다. / 그런 다음 양자 Circuit을 실행하고 투영값을 측정합니다.
examples.why: circuit is 양자 회로 at line 34 but bare English 'Circuit' from Step 2 onward (including the heading '### 양자 Circuit'); gate and backend are likewise left as capitalized English inside Korean sentences. Same concept split across two renderings within one file.

examples.source: PQKs offer potential advantages over standard quantum kernels, particularly for near-term quantum hardware. … while remaining more practical for near-term devices.
examples.suggested: PQK는 특히 단기(near-term) 양자 하드웨어에서 … 단기 양자 장치에 더 실용적으로 활용될 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: PQK는 특히 근시일 내(near-term) 양자 하드웨어에서 … 근시일 내 장치에 더 실용적으로 활용될 수 있습니다.
examples.why: '근시일 내' is a literal calque of 'near-term' meaning 'within a few days' in ordinary Korean; as a prenominal modifier of 하드웨어/장치 it reads as machine translation. Korean quantum writing uses 단기 or 근미래 for the NISQ-era sense.

examples.source: If you found this work interesting, you might be interested in the following material:
examples.suggested: 이 내용이 흥미로웠다면, 다음 자료도 살펴보세요:
examples.translation: 이 내용이 흥미로우셨다면, 다음 자료도 살펴보시기 바랍니다:
examples.why: '-으셨다면' plus '-시기 바랍니다' is honorific/formal-request register, out of step with the plain instructional tone used everywhere else in the file (e.g. '확인하세요' at line 40). A localized formal slip, not a systemic one.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the hard conceptual passages (SSVQE weight-priority argument, VQD penalty/deflation chain, QSR Fourier sampling) teach as clearly as the English — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, "anda" register holds. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "overlap" is split within the file between "pertindanan" (VQD intro, theoretical-layout bullets) and "pertindihan" (Implementation, fidelity, betas paragraphs); "eigenstate" is mostly "keadaan eigen" but line 421 leaves the bare English "eigenstate bertenaga lebih rendah"; "ortogon"/"ortogonal" also alternate. (2) "minimization" gets three renderings — "pengecilan fungsi kos", "rutin pengecilan", and the odd non-standard "penganggitan minimum" (line 530) — where "peminimuman" is the natural term and is what the surrounding verbs ("meminimumkan") already use. (3) "mengsampel" (lines 551, 553) is malformed morphology; standard Malay is "mensampel" / "mengambil sampel", and the file's own noun "pensampelan" is correct. (4) "periodicity" is rendered "kekerapan" (frequency) rather than "keberkalaan" — a related but different property of the cost function. (5) Glossary leaks read as machine substitution: "Kita akan men-transpil Circuit…" and "Circuit kuantum baharu" / "Backend yang kita pilih" where a Malay quantum writer writes "litar". None of these would cause a learner to form a false belief.

examples.source: …the contribution of each overlap term to the cost… / a function for an overlap penalty… / any overlap between the current variational state and the lower-energy eigenstates
examples.suggested: Pick one: "pertindihan" throughout; and "keadaan eigen bertenaga lebih rendah" instead of the bare English "eigenstate".
examples.translation: …sumbangan setiap sebutan pertindanan kepada kos… / fungsi untuk penalti pertindihan… / sebarang pertindihan antara keadaan variasi semasa dan eigenstate bertenaga lebih rendah
examples.why: "overlap" — the central quantity of the whole VQD section — is rendered two ways within one lesson, and "eigenstate" reverts to English in a single sentence after being "keadaan eigen" everywhere else. Recognizable, but a reader tracking the penalty term across the theory and the code sections sees two different words for the same object.

examples.source: Because the cost function minimization is highly iterative… / the minimization routine successfully terminated… / all three minimizations converged
examples.suggested: peminimuman fungsi kos … rutin peminimuman … ketiga-tiga peminimuman telah menumpu
examples.translation: Oleh kerana pengecilan fungsi kos sangat berulang… / rutin pengecilan berjaya ditamatkan… / ketiga-tiga penganggitan minimum telah menumpu
examples.why: Three renderings of one term, one of which ("penganggitan") is not standard Malay and does not correspond to any established mathematical term, while the file's own verb is "meminimumkan". "Pengecilan" (shrinking) is also weaker than the mathematical sense of minimization.

examples.source: The next step is to sample the cost function C(θ) multiple times… we will need to sample the cost function 2S+1 times.
examples.suggested: …ialah mensampel (atau: mengambil sampel bagi) fungsi kos $C(\theta)$ beberapa kali… kita perlu mengambil sampel fungsi kos sebanyak $2S+1$ kali.
examples.translation: Langkah seterusnya ialah mengsampel fungsi kos $C(\theta)$ beberapa kali… kita perlu mengsampel fungsi kos sebanyak $2S+1$ kali.
examples.why: "mengsampel" violates Malay meN- prefix assimilation (meN- + s → men-); no native technical writer would produce it, especially in a file that already uses the correct derived noun "pensampelan".

examples.source: Depending on the periodicity and bandwidth of the original function, the set S may be finite or infinite.
examples.suggested: Bergantung pada keberkalaan dan lebar jalur fungsi asal, …
examples.translation: Bergantung pada kekerapan dan lebar jalur fungsi asal, set $S$ mungkin terhingga atau tak terhingga.
examples.why: "kekerapan" means frequency, not periodicity. In the QSR derivation the two are distinct properties of the cost function, and "lebar jalur" (bandwidth) already covers the frequency-content side, so the pair loses its distinction.

examples.source: We will transpile the circuit using the preset pass manager… / that new circuit must also be transpiled… to run on the backend we select.
examples.suggested: Kita akan mentranspil litar itu menggunakan pengurus laluan pratetap… / litar baharu itu juga perlu ditranspilasi… pada backend yang kita pilih.
examples.translation: Kita akan men-transpil Circuit menggunakan preset pass manager… / Circuit baharu itu juga perlu ditranspilasi… untuk dijalankan pada Backend yang kita pilih.
examples.why: "Circuit" and "Backend" are capitalized mid-sentence as if pasted from a glossary, while the same paragraph happily translates the surrounding prose; Malay quantum writing uses "litar" for circuit. Reads as machine substitution rather than authored text.

examples.source: Note that transpilation has been built in to the `calculate_overlaps` or `cost_func_vqd` functions.
examples.suggested: (flagging for the record, not a fix request) — keep the negated Malay, but note the divergence from the EN string.
examples.translation: Perhatikan bahawa transpilasi belum dibina ke dalam fungsi `calculate_overlaps` atau `cost_func_vqd`.
examples.why: The Malay negates the English sentence. Recorded here for completeness only: the English source is self-contradictory (it invites the reader to "build in this additional transpilation" in the very next sentence, and the shown code contains no transpilation), so the Malay states what is actually true and does NOT mislead the learner — it is the EN line that is defective.

editor_note: The file is clearly a two-pass merge and several of the splits are actively misleading, not merely inconsistent. "Sparsity" is rendered throughout the first half as "kekurangan" (= deficiency/shortage), so "the objective balances accuracy with sparsity" becomes "mengimbangi ketepatan dengan kekurangan" and "tuning sparsity" becomes "menyetel kekurangan" — a learner is taught that regularization trades accuracy against a shortage rather than against how few learners stay active; the second half switches to the closer "jarangnya". "Regularization" is likewise split: "penggularisasian" (a coinage; standard Malay is "regularisasi") in Steps 1–3, but "pengaturan semula" (= rearrangement/re-setting) from Step 4 on ("λ=7 … pengaturan semula", "α-pengaturan semula adaptif"), which names a completely different operation. Two separate sentences drop "exponentially" and replace it with "terlalu besar" (= too large), inverting the point: "meneroka subset peramal yang terlalu besar" and "meneroka ruang carian yang terlalu besar dengan lebih cekap" now say the spaces are too big, where the English says their exponential size is exactly what the quantum step can handle. Finally, the Background metric list collapses accuracy and precision into "bandingkan ketepatan, ketepatan, ingatan semula, dan F1" — "precision" disappears as a distinct metric, though the rest of the file correctly uses "presisi"; the same two-pass split also gives "pemelajar" vs "peramal" for weak learners and "litar" vs an untranslated capitalised "Circuit" ("lebar Circuit", "kedalaman Circuit").

examples.source: the objective balances accuracy with sparsity through a regularization term … before scaling width or tuning sparsity
examples.suggested: objektif mengimbangi ketepatan dengan kejarangan melalui sebutan regularisasi … sebelum menaikkan lebar atau menala kejarangan
examples.translation: objektif mengimbangi ketepatan dengan kekurangan melalui sebutan penggularisasian … sebelum menaikkan lebar atau menyetel kekurangan
examples.why: "kekurangan" means deficiency/shortage, not sparsity. The learner is taught that the objective trades accuracy against a "shortage" and that one "tunes a deficiency", losing the actual concept (how few weak learners remain active). Used this way ~8 times in Steps 1–3, while Step 4 onward uses the closer "jarangnya".

examples.source: Regularization introduces additional nuance: a fixed λ=7 enforces consistent sparsity … whereas adaptive α-regularization automatically tunes sparsity
examples.suggested: Regularisasi memperkenalkan nuansa tambahan: λ=7 yang tetap menguatkuasakan kejarangan yang konsisten … manakala regularisasi-α adaptif secara automatik menala kejarangan
examples.translation: Pengaturan semula memperkenalkan nuansa tambahan: λ=7 yang tetap menguatkuasakan jarangnya yang konsisten … manakala pengaturan semula α-adaptif secara automatik menala jarangnya
examples.why: "pengaturan semula" means rearrangement / re-setting — a different operation entirely. Combined with "penggularisasian" in the first half, the same parameter (`regularization`, and the whole "### Penggularisasian" section) is named two unrelated ways, and the Step 4 name teaches a false concept.

examples.source: explore exponentially large subsets of learners simultaneously in superposition … can explore these exponentially large search spaces more efficiently
examples.suggested: meneroka subset pemelajar yang besar secara eksponen … boleh meneroka ruang carian yang besar secara eksponen ini dengan lebih cekap
examples.translation: meneroka subset peramal yang terlalu besar secara serentak dalam superposisi … boleh meneroka ruang carian yang terlalu besar dengan lebih cekap
examples.why: "exponentially large" is replaced by "terlalu besar" (= too large / excessively large), which reads as a limitation and contradicts the sentence's own claim that the quantum step handles these spaces efficiently. The file proves it knows the right phrase — line ~602 correctly has "berskala secara eksponen".

examples.source: and compare accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 across all runs
examples.suggested: dan bandingkan ketepatan, presisi, ingatan semula, dan F1 merentas semua larian
examples.translation: dan bandingkan ketepatan, ketepatan, ingatan semula, dan F1 merentas semua larian
examples.why: Accuracy and precision are both rendered "ketepatan", so the list reads as a duplicated word and "precision" vanishes as a distinct metric in the one place the tutorial first introduces the four it will compare. Lines ~167 and ~491 correctly use "presisi".

examples.source: weak learners / learners
examples.suggested: pemelajar lemah / pemelajar throughout
examples.translation: peramal lemah, peramal (Step 4 onward) vs pemelajar lemah, pemelajar (Background–Step 3)
examples.why: "peramal" means forecaster/predictor, a different role from a learner in an ensemble, and the switch happens exactly at the two-pass seam. The same seam also leaves "litar" (Steps 2–3) against an untranslated capitalised "Circuit" in "lebar Circuit" and "kedalaman Circuit", plus "klasik" vs "klasikal" and "larian" vs "jalaran".

examples.source: weaker models such as linear regressors are typically pruned
examples.suggested: model yang lebih lemah seperti model regresi linear biasanya dipangkas
examples.translation: model yang lebih lemah seperti pengresor linear biasanya dipangkas
examples.why: "pengresor" is not a Malay word — it is an English stem with a Malay prefix bolted on, and a native technical writer would write "model regresi linear" or simply "regresi linear".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and no passage teaches a false concept, but a native technical editor would change several things. The biggest is a glossary-substitution leak: "circuits" is left as bare English "Circuit" in four places ("Mając już gotowe Circuit", "transpilację Circuit", "Po zoptymalizowaniu Circuit", "głębokość Circuit") even though the same file correctly writes "obwody kwantowe"/"obwód kwantowy" everywhere in sections 0–1. "Krylov" is likewise split within the file — undeclined "przestrzeń/wymiar Krylov" in sections 0–1 versus declined "wymiaru/bazy/przestrzeni Kryłowa" in sections 4–5. Two grammatical slips a native would never write: "to przestrzeń rozpiętą przez wektory" (accusative for nominative "rozpięta") and "będziemy rozpiąć podprzestrzenie" (perfective infinitive after "będziemy"; must be "rozpinać"). Terminology nits: "antysferromagnetyczny" (twice) is a malformed "antyferromagnetyczny"; "postselection" becomes "selekcja wstępna" (literally *pre*-selection — the inline gloss rescues it, but "postselekcja" is the standard term); "preset pass manager" becomes "menedżer przejść", where compiler "pass" is read as "przejście"; and "overlap" is consistently "pokrycie" rather than the usual "przekrycie/przekrywanie". Finally, the intro drops "provably" from "provably and efficiently converges", rendering it as the near-tautological "zbieżnie i efektywnie dąży" — the provable-convergence claim is SKQD's selling point and survives elsewhere ("dowodliwie wystarczający", "posiada gwarancje zbieżności"), so this is a dropped qualifier rather than a misleading statement. Informal "ty" register holds ("Przeczytaj poniższe pytania, zastanów się…"); no Pan/Pani slips.

examples.source: Now that we have created the circuits, we can optimize them for a target hardware. … we transpile the circuits … After optimizing the circuits for hardware execution … To keep circuit depths low
examples.suggested: Mając już gotowe obwody, możemy je zoptymalizować … transpilację obwodów … Po zoptymalizowaniu obwodów … głębokość obwodów
examples.translation: Mając już gotowe Circuit, możemy je zoptymalizować … Teraz wykonujemy transpilację Circuit … Po zoptymalizowaniu Circuit … Aby utrzymać głębokość Circuit na niskim poziomie
examples.why: Bare English 'Circuit' (singular, capitalised, undeclined) reads as a glossary-substitution artifact, not Polish. The same file translates the term correctly as 'obwody kwantowe' in sections 0–1, so the term is split within the file.

examples.source: we will span subspaces for increasing Krylov dimension / the space spanned by vectors obtained by multiplying…
examples.suggested: będziemy rozpinać podprzestrzenie … / to przestrzeń rozpięta przez wektory…
examples.translation: będziemy rozpiąć podprzestrzenie dla rosnących wymiarów Kryłowa / to przestrzeń rozpiętą przez wektory otrzymane przez mnożenie…
examples.why: 'będziemy rozpiąć' is ungrammatical (perfective infinitive after the future auxiliary; must be imperfective 'rozpinać'), and 'przestrzeń rozpiętą' puts the participle in the accusative where the nominative 'rozpięta' is required. Both are errors no Polish technical writer would produce.

examples.source: The algorithm provably and efficiently converges to the ground state, under the assumptions described in lesson 2.
examples.suggested: Algorytm w sposób dowodliwy i efektywnie zbiega do stanu podstawowego, przy założeniach opisanych w lekcji 2.
examples.translation: Algorytm zbieżnie i efektywnie dąży do stanu podstawowego, przy założeniach opisanych w lekcji 2.
examples.why: 'provably' is dropped and replaced by the near-tautological adverb 'zbieżnie' ('convergently converges'). Provable convergence is the whole point of SKQD over SQD, so the lesson's headline claim is flattened — a dropped qualifier rather than a false statement.

examples.source: one can use a problem-specific postselection routine (for example, filter out bitstrings that do not adhere to problem-specific patterns)
examples.suggested: można zastosować postselekcję specyficzną dla problemu (…)
examples.translation: można zastosować selekcję wstępną specyficzną dla problemu (na przykład odfiltrowanie ciągów bitów niespełniających wzorców charakterystycznych dla problemu)
examples.why: 'selekcja wstępna' literally means pre-selection, inverting the temporal prefix of postselection — filtering happens after sampling, as the code `postselect_counts` shows. The inline parenthetical still describes the correct operation, so it mislabels rather than misteaches, but 'postselekcja' is the standard Polish term.

examples.source: it is wise to address lattice problems which are amenable to pre-fault tolerant hardware / Ref [2] showed that…
examples.suggested: warto zajmować się problemami sieciowymi, które nadają się do sprzętu z ery przed korekcją błędów / Praca [\[2\]](#references) wykazała, że…
examples.translation: warto podejmować problemy sieciowe podatne na sprzęt przed osiągnięciem tolerancji na błędy / Ref [\[2\]](#references) wykazał, że…
examples.why: 'podatne na sprzęt' calques 'amenable to' as 'susceptible to' and reads as nonsense; the whole clause is a word-order tracing of the English. 'Ref' is left in English where 'Praca'/'Publikacja' is idiomatic — with the wrong gender agreement ('wykazał' vs 'wykazała') that follows from it.

editor_note: The Background paragraph inverts a deliberately modest scope claim: English "a quadratic speedup over a handful of classical algorithms" becomes "kwadratowego przyspieszenia względem wielu klasycznych algorytmów" ("over MANY classical algorithms"), teaching the learner that amplitude amplification broadly speeds up many classical algorithms — the exact misconception the English hedge guards against. On top of that, the glossary protection has damaged the core term throughout: "qubit" is capitalized mid-sentence and glued into Polish compounds as "na $N$ Qubitach", "trójQubitowej", "dwu-Qubitowych", "liczbą Qubitów" — no Polish technical writer would write this (the conventional form is "kubit"/"kubitach", "trójkubitowej", "dwukubitowych"). Two more English words leak untranslated and clash with the file's own choices: "Gate kontrolowana-Z" and "Gate `MCMT`" against "bramka" used everywhere else, and the heading "Pełny Circuit Grovera" against "obwód" used everywhere else. Also "Primityw `Sampler`" (line 35) is a misspelling of, and inconsistent with, "prymityw(u)" used at lines 24, 168 and 170, and "algorytmy bliskie czasom współczesnym" is a stiff calque of "near-term algorithms".

examples.source: Amplitude amplification is a general-purpose quantum algorithm, or subroutine, that can be used to obtain a quadratic speedup over a handful of classical algorithms.
examples.suggested: ... do uzyskania kwadratowego przyspieszenia względem garstki (niewielkiej liczby) klasycznych algorytmów.
examples.translation: Wzmocnienie amplitudy to ogólny algorytm kwantowy (lub podprogram), który można wykorzystać do uzyskania kwadratowego przyspieszenia względem wielu klasycznych algorytmów.
examples.why: Quantity reversal that strengthens the claim: 'a handful' (a small, limited set) becomes 'wielu' (many). The English hedge is pedagogically load-bearing — it tells the learner that quadratic speedup applies only to a narrow class of classical algorithms. The Polish teaches the opposite scope.

examples.source: a multi-controlled generalization over $N$ qubits ... a three-qubit computational space ... two-qubit gate depths ... with the number of qubits
examples.suggested: na $N$ kubitach ... w trójkubitowej przestrzeni obliczeniowej ... głębokości bramek dwukubitowych ... wraz z liczbą kubitów
examples.translation: wielokrotnie kontrolowane uogólnienie na $N$ Qubitach ... w trójQubitowej przestrzeni obliczeniowej ... głębokości obwodów dwu-Qubitowych ... wraz z liczbą Qubitów
examples.why: Glossary-protection artifact: the term is capitalized mid-sentence and spliced into Polish compounds and inflections ('trójQubitowej', 'dwu-Qubitowych', 'Qubicie'). Recognizable, so not misleading, but no native Polish technical writer would produce these forms; it reads as machine output on every occurrence.

examples.source: A controlled-Z gate ... The `MCMT` gate is used to implement the multi-controlled Z-gate. / ### Full Grover circuit
examples.suggested: Bramka kontrolowana-Z ... Bramka `MCMT` służy ... / ### Pełny obwód Grovera
examples.translation: Gate kontrolowana-Z ... Gate `MCMT` służy do implementacji wielokrotnie kontrolowanej bramki Z. / ### Pełny Circuit Grovera
examples.why: English 'Gate' and 'Circuit' are left untranslated in exactly the places where the same file otherwise uses 'bramka' (bramek X, bramki Z, bramki Hadamarda) and 'obwód' (obwód wyroczni, obwody Grovera). Within-file inconsistency on two core terms; 'Gate kontrolowana-Z' additionally mixes an English noun with a Polish feminine adjective.

examples.source: The runtime `Sampler` primitive allows seamless execution of Grover circuits.
examples.suggested: Prymityw `Sampler` środowiska uruchomieniowego umożliwia płynne wykonywanie obwodów Grovera.
examples.translation: Primityw `Sampler` środowiska uruchomieniowego umożliwia bezproblemowe wykonywanie obwodów Grovera.
examples.why: 'Primityw' is not a Polish word — it is a typo for 'prymityw', which the same file uses correctly at lines 24, 168 and 170. Also 'środowiska uruchomieniowego' here vs. 'środowiska Qiskit Runtime' at line 24 for the same referent.

examples.source: give near-term examples of optimization with quantum computers / For a more in-depth look at near-term algorithms
examples.suggested: pokazują przykłady optymalizacji na komputerach kwantowych w bliskiej perspektywie (near-term) / ... na algorytmy krótkoterminowe (near-term)
examples.translation: dają przykłady optymalizacji bliskiej czasom współczesnym z użyciem komputerów kwantowych / Aby uzyskać głębsze spojrzenie na algorytmy bliskie czasom współczesnym
examples.why: 'bliski czasom współczesnym' is a literal calque of 'near-term' that reads as 'close to contemporary times' and, in the first sentence, attaches to 'optymalizacji' rather than to the hardware era — stiff and slightly confusing. Polish technical writing keeps 'near-term' or uses 'w bliskiej perspektywie czasowej'.

examples.source: marks the $2^{N}-1$ state (`'1'`\*$N$ bit-string)
examples.suggested: oznacza stan $2^{N}-1$ (ciąg bitów `'1'`\*$N$)
examples.translation: oznacza stan $2^{N}-1$ (`'1'`\*$N$ bitów)
examples.why: 'bit-string' is reduced to 'bitów', so the gloss reads '(1 times N bits)' — a count of bits rather than the bit-string made of N ones. Small dropped qualifier; the parenthetical no longer explains what it was there to explain.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every date, qubit count, name and "Verdadeiro ou falso" answer matches the English, and core terms are right (porta/taxa de erro de porta, qubits supercondutores, BQP → "tempo polinomial quântico com erro limitado", medições em meio ao circuito). What a native technical editor would change: (1) "quantum-centric supercomputing" is rendered "supercomputação quântica centrada" in all three places (lines 66, 120 ×2) — "centrada" is left dangling with no complement; PT needs "supercomputação centrada em (computação) quântica"; (2) the 2015 image caption writes "computador quântico superconductor" — an English/Spanish non-word, inconsistent with the correct "supercondutores" used at lines 93 and 120; (3) "hybrid multi-cloud" becomes the orphan adjective "e híbrida multi-cloud" at line 142 (no noun to agree with — should be "nuvem híbrida multi-cloud"); plus two calques: "ele encerrou famosamente seu discurso" (line 88) and the heading "Ecossistema quântico escalando" (line 53). None of these would make a learner believe something false, so this is MINOR, not FAIL.

examples.source: We call this vision of connected quantum and classical quantum-centric supercomputing.
examples.suggested: ... de supercomputação centrada em computação quântica.
examples.translation: Chamamos essa visão de computadores quânticos e clássicos conectados de supercomputação quântica centrada.
examples.why: "quantum-centric" is an adjective meaning quantum sits at the centre of the workflow; "quântica centrada" leaves "centrada" without a complement and reads as broken Portuguese. Same malformed term recurs twice more in the 2022 row ("era de supercomputação quântica centrada", "concretizar a supercomputação quântica centrada"). Recognizable, so MINOR.

examples.source: Layout of the IBM four-qubit superconducting quantum computer announced in 2015.
examples.suggested: Layout do computador quântico supercondutor de quatro qubits da IBM anunciado em 2015.
examples.translation: Layout do computador quântico superconductor de quatro qubits da IBM anunciado em 2015.
examples.why: "superconductor" is not a Portuguese word (English/Spanish leak) and is inconsistent with "qubits supercondutores" used correctly in the 2005 and 2022 rows.

examples.source: Readiness includes adoption of enabling technologies such as automation, AI, and hybrid multi-cloud;
examples.suggested: ... como automação, IA e nuvem híbrida multi-cloud;
examples.translation: A prontidão inclui a adoção de tecnologias habilitadoras, como automação, IA e híbrida multi-cloud;
examples.why: "híbrida" is a feminine adjective with no noun to modify — the English noun phrase "hybrid multi-cloud" was transferred word-for-word and the head noun vanished, leaving ungrammatical Portuguese in a list.

examples.source: he famously closed his keynote speech with the statement
examples.suggested: ele encerrou seu célebre discurso com a frase / ficou famoso por encerrar seu discurso com a frase
examples.translation: ele encerrou famosamente seu discurso de abertura com a declaração
examples.why: "famosamente" is a direct calque of the English sentence adverb "famously", which Portuguese does not use this way; a native technical writer would recast it with "célebre" or "ficou famoso por".

examples.source: **Quantum ecosystem scaling** – Open innovation fosters collaborative learning.
examples.suggested: **Escalabilidade do ecossistema quântico** – ...
examples.translation: **Ecossistema quântico escalando** – A inovação aberta fomenta o aprendizado colaborativo.
examples.why: The English gerund headline is carried over literally; "Ecossistema quântico escalando" reads as a progressive verb phrase rather than a section label. Portuguese headings of this kind use a nominalization ("Escalabilidade"/"Expansão do ecossistema quântico").

editor_note: No semantic drift: every quantity, condition and caveat survives intact ($T_2 \le 2 T_1$, "reinicialize para 1 em vez de 0 com probabilidade `p_reset`", the qubits [0,1] vs [1,0] ordering note, the $P(A|B)$ recorded-vs-true bit distinction). Terminology is consistent and defensible — "gate" is kept in English throughout ("erros de gate", "gates de base", "tempo de gate", "gate de dois qubits"), qubit/backend/reset/bit-flip stay English, "relaxamento térmico"/"defasagem"/"amortecimento de amplitude" are the right domain renderings, and "você" holds with no formal slips. What a native editor would fix: two sentences drop the required preposition before the relative — "quais qubits ele deve ser aplicado" (needs "a quais qubits") and "independentemente de quais qubits ela age" (needs "sobre quais qubits"); "escrever sua própria transpiler pass" is a half-translated code-switch with a mismatched Portuguese determiner on an English noun; "um canal de erro CPTP de n-qubits em geral" misplaces the modifier so "geral" reads as the adverbial "in general" rather than qualifying the channel; and the H2 "Adicionando erros a um modelo de ruído" breaks the infinitive heading convention used everywhere else ("Inicializar", "Combinar", "Converter", "Executar").

examples.source: we must specify the type of *instruction* that it acts on and what qubits to apply it to
examples.suggested: devemos especificar o tipo de *instrução* sobre a qual ele age e a quais qubits ele deve ser aplicado
examples.translation: devemos especificar o tipo de *instrução* sobre a qual ele age e quais qubits ele deve ser aplicado
examples.why: Missing the preposition 'a' before the relative makes the second clause ungrammatical; a native writer would never drop it after 'ser aplicado'.

examples.source: regardless of which qubits it acts on
examples.suggested: independentemente de sobre quais qubits ela age
examples.translation: independentemente de quais qubits ela age
examples.why: 'agir' requires 'sobre'; the calqued English 'which qubits it acts on' left the preposition stranded and then deleted.

examples.source: you should [write your own transpiler pass](/guides/custom-transpiler-pass) (`TransformationPass`)
examples.suggested: você deve [escrever seu próprio passe de transpilação](/guides/custom-transpiler-pass) (`TransformationPass`)
examples.translation: você deve [escrever sua própria transpiler pass](/guides/custom-transpiler-pass) (`TransformationPass`)
examples.why: Half-translated: a Portuguese feminine determiner glued onto an untranslated English noun phrase. The concept is still recognizable, but the mixed agreement reads as raw MT.

examples.source: a general n-qubit CPTP error channel given as a list of Kraus matrices
examples.suggested: um canal de erro CPTP geral de n qubits, dado como uma lista de matrizes de Kraus
examples.translation: um canal de erro CPTP de n-qubits em geral, dado como uma lista de matrizes de Kraus
examples.why: 'em geral' parses as the sentence adverb 'in general' instead of the adjective qualifying the channel; the adjective 'geral' must sit with 'canal'.

examples.source: ## Add errors to a noise model
examples.suggested: ## Adicionar erros a um modelo de ruído
examples.translation: ## Adicionando erros a um modelo de ruído
examples.why: Every other section heading in the file uses the infinitive (Inicializar, Combinar, Converter, Executar, Construir); this lone gerund breaks the page's heading convention.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, the Grover-operation and OR-gate definitions match the English exactly, and the informal "tu" register holds consistently ("Observă", "Alege", "Rulează", "Interoghează", no dumneavoastră). Core terminology is correct and stable (poartă de interogare în fază, retroacțiune de fază, qubit/qubiți, operația Grover, stările bazei standard). What a native editor would change: (1) "circuit cuantic" is capitalized mid-sentence as "Circuit cuantic" in five places (lines 59, 75, 81 twice, 83) while line 58 correctly has it lowercase — a glossary-substitution artifact that is both wrong orthography and an inconsistency within the same paragraph; (2) "all-zero state" is left half-English as "starea all-zero" (line 69) in the otherwise fully translated algorithm box; (3) "To be clear" is rendered "Spre a fi clar" (line 56), an archaic/stiff construction no Romanian technical writer would use — "Ca să fie clar" is the natural form; (4) "discarded" becomes "ignorat" (line 34), which says the workspace qubit is *ignored* rather than discarded/released — recognizable but the wrong shade. Also cosmetic: the quotation on line 96 opens with Romanian „ but closes with a straight ".

examples.source: can therefore be implemented by a quantum circuit having no query gates / Here is a quantum circuit representation of the Grover operation
examples.suggested: printr-un circuit cuantic ... / o reprezentare sub formă de circuit cuantic
examples.translation: poate fi implementată printr-un Circuit cuantic fără nicio poartă de interogare / Iată o reprezentare ca Circuit cuantic a operației Grover
examples.why: "Circuit cuantic" is capitalized mid-sentence in five places, while line 58 has the correct lowercase "circuit cuantic" — a glossary-substitution artifact producing both a spelling error and within-file inconsistency for the single most common term in the file.

examples.source: Initialize an $n$ qubit register $\mathsf{Q}$ to the all-zero state $\vert 0^n \rangle$
examples.suggested: Inițializează un registru de $n$ qubiți $\mathsf{Q}$ în starea cu toți biții zero $\vert 0^n \rangle$
examples.translation: Inițializează un registru de $n$ qubiți $\mathsf{Q}$ în starea all-zero $\vert 0^n \rangle$
examples.why: "all-zero" is left in English inside an otherwise fully translated numbered algorithm step; "starea all-zero" is not Romanian and is trivially translatable.

examples.source: To be clear, this is how $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ operates on standard basis states
examples.suggested: Ca să fie clar, acesta este modul în care $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ operează pe stările bazei standard
examples.translation: Spre a fi clar, acesta este modul în care $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ operează pe stările bazei standard
examples.why: "Spre a fi clar" is an archaic supine construction that reads as literal MT; a Romanian technical writer would use "Ca să fie clar" / "Pentru claritate".

examples.source: can be reused (to implement subsequent $Z_f$ gates, for instance) or simply discarded
examples.suggested: ... sau pur și simplu eliminat / lăsat deoparte
examples.translation: poate fi reutilizat (de exemplu, pentru a implementa porți $Z_f$ ulterioare) sau pur și simplu ignorat
examples.why: "discarded" (the qubit is released/no longer needed) becomes "ignorat" (ignored), which suggests the qubit stays around but is disregarded — a recognizable but imprecise shade, not enough to mislead about the physics.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted claims; the error-hierarchy sentence ("erorile de citire tind să fie mai mari decât cele ale operațiunii cu 2 qubiți, care la rândul lor...") and the QPU-access caveat are both exact, and informal "tu" holds ("Accesul tău", "Te rog să calculezi"). What a native editor would change: (1) "gate" is left in English and capitalized mid-sentence four times ("Gate-ul de entanglare cu 2 qubiți", "erorile Gate-urilor", "Gate-urile „sx" și „ecr""), against this project's own ro glossary (gate → preferred "poartă", "Gate" listed as leaked_en) and against every sibling lesson in the same course, which uses "poartă"; (2) "lecture pdf" is rendered "PDF-ul cu lectura acestei lecții" — "lectură" in Romanian means *reading*, not *prelegere/curs*, a classic false friend; (3) "jupyter notebooks" is over-translated as "caietele Jupyter", where Romanian technical writing keeps "notebook-uri Jupyter"; (4) "As you can see" is calqued twice as "Cum poți vedea / Cum poți observa" instead of the idiomatic "După cum poți vedea". Also mildly off-register: "operațiune" (business/administrative) where technical Romanian uses "operație" — consistent, so cosmetic only.

examples.source: Edges indicate pairs to which you can directly apply the 2-qubit entangling gate. / We now turn to gate errors. / the median errors for the 'sx' and the 'ecr' gates
examples.suggested: ...le poți aplica direct poarta de întricare cu 2 qubiți. / ...către erorile porților. / ...pentru porțile „sx" și „ecr"
examples.translation: Muchiile indică perechile cărora le poți aplica direct Gate-ul de entanglare cu 2 qubiți. / Acum ne îndreptăm atenția către erorile Gate-urilor. / erorile mediane pentru Gate-urile „sx" și „ecr"
examples.why: The repo's own translation/glossary/ro.json sets gate → preferred "poartă" and flags "Gate" as an English leak; sibling files in this same course (bits-gates-and-circuits, teleportation) use "poartă". Keeping the English noun and capitalizing it mid-sentence is a glossary leak plus a within-course inconsistency. Recognizable, so MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: This lesson's lecture pdf was split into two parts.
examples.suggested: PDF-ul prelegerii acestei lecții a fost împărțit în două părți.
examples.translation: PDF-ul cu lectura acestei lecții a fost împărțit în două părți.
examples.why: False friend: Romanian "lectură" means *reading/perusal*, never *lecture*. The correct term for a taught lecture is "prelegere" (or "curs"). The reader still finds the download links, so it does not mislead pedagogically, but a native writer would never say "PDF-ul cu lectura".

examples.source: You already used the first two in the previous jupyter notebooks.
examples.suggested: Le-ai folosit deja pe primele două în notebook-urile Jupyter anterioare.
examples.translation: Le-ai folosit deja pe primele două în caietele Jupyter anterioare.
examples.why: "caiet" is the school-exercise-book sense of "notebook"; Romanian Qiskit/data-science writing keeps "notebook Jupyter". An over-translation of a term the field leaves in English — the opposite direction from the "Gate" leak above, which is why the file reads inconsistently.

examples.source: As you can see, nodes are qubits which are numbered. / As you can see, the errors of readout tend to be larger...
examples.suggested: După cum poți vedea, ... / După cum poți observa, ...
examples.translation: Cum poți vedea, nodurile sunt qubiți numerotați. / Cum poți observa, erorile de citire tind să fie mai mari...
examples.why: Bare "Cum poți vedea" is a direct calque of "As you can see"; idiomatic Romanian requires "După cum...". Grammatical but audibly translated, twice in the same file.

editor_note: No misleading content: the technical substance is faithful throughout (circuit depth = 9, 156 qubits vs. billions of classical bits, coherence time 200-300 μs, transpiled two-qubit depth 80+, circuit cutting vs. knitting all land correctly), the English-retained term convention (qubit / gate / layer / circuit depth / entangling layer / Estimator / backend / transpilation) is consistent, and the informal register holds with no ครับ/ค่ะ. What a native editor would change: the English impersonal pronoun "one" is calqued as the Thai numeral หนึ่ง four times ("หนึ่งอ้างถึง 'layer' ของ gate", "ซึ่งหนึ่งจงใจนำ gate ที่ simplify ไปเป็น identity", "สังเกตว่าหนึ่งสามารถเรียก CNOT แต่ละตัวว่า 'layer'") — หนึ่ง is never an impersonal subject in Thai, so these sentences read as raw MT and momentarily parse as the number 1. Smaller items: "unique to quantum computing" → "ที่ไม่ซ้ำกันกับควอนตัมคอมพิวติ้ง" (reads as "not duplicated with", not "found only in"); "orders of magnitude faster than RAM" flattened to "เร็วกว่า RAM หลายเท่า" ("several times faster"); "substantial queue times" → "เวลาคิวที่มีนัยสำคัญ" (borrows the statistical sense of "significant"); and a doubled term in "ตรวจสอบ transpiled two-qubit depth ที่ถูก transpile".

examples.source: In quantum computing, one refers to a "layer" of gates which can all be executed simultaneously. … in which one intentionally implements gates that simplify to an identity … Note that one can call each CNOT a "layer" on its own
examples.suggested: ในควอนตัมคอมพิวติ้ง เราเรียกกลุ่มของ gate ที่ดำเนินการพร้อมกันได้ว่า "layer" … ซึ่งเราจงใจใส่ gate ที่ยุบรวมเป็น identity … สังเกตว่าเราสามารถนับ CNOT แต่ละตัวเป็น "layer" ของตัวเอง
examples.translation: ในควอนตัมคอมพิวติ้ง หนึ่งอ้างถึง "layer" ของ gate ที่สามารถดำเนินการพร้อมกันได้ … ซึ่งหนึ่งจงใจนำ gate ที่ simplify ไปเป็น identity … สังเกตว่าหนึ่งสามารถเรียก CNOT แต่ละตัวว่า "layer" ของตัวเอง
examples.why: English impersonal "one" calqued as the Thai numeral หนึ่ง. Thai has no impersonal pronoun หนึ่ง; a reader first parses it as the number 1 and the clause reads as machine output. Native technical Thai uses เรา or an agentless construction. Occurs four times in this section.

examples.source: One step in resource estimation that is unique to quantum computing is the circuit depth.
examples.suggested: ขั้นตอนหนึ่งในการประมาณทรัพยากรที่มีเฉพาะในควอนตัมคอมพิวติ้งคือ circuit depth
examples.translation: ขั้นตอนหนึ่งในการประมาณทรัพยากรที่ไม่ซ้ำกันกับควอนตัมคอมพิวติ้งคือ circuit depth
examples.why: "Unique to X" rendered with ไม่ซ้ำกันกับ, which means "not duplicated with / not identical to" — the wrong sense of "unique". Meaning is still recoverable from context, but the phrase is a false-friend rendering a native writer would replace with มีเฉพาะใน / เป็นเอกลักษณ์ของ.

examples.source: L1 is the smallest and fastest while L3 is the largest and slowest, but still orders of magnitude faster than RAM.
examples.suggested: … แต่ยังคงเร็วกว่า RAM หลายลำดับขนาด (orders of magnitude)
examples.translation: L1 มีขนาดเล็กที่สุดและเร็วที่สุด ในขณะที่ L3 ใหญ่ที่สุดและช้าที่สุด แต่ยังคงเร็วกว่า RAM หลายเท่า
examples.why: "Orders of magnitude" flattened to หลายเท่า ("several times"). The pedagogical point — that even the slowest cache is in a different league from RAM — is weakened; the learner takes away a factor of a few instead of 100x+.

examples.source: quantum computers might have substantial queue times
examples.suggested: คอมพิวเตอร์ควอนตัมอาจมีเวลาคิวที่ยาวนานพอสมควร
examples.translation: คอมพิวเตอร์ควอนตัมอาจมีเวลาคิวที่มีนัยสำคัญ
examples.why: มีนัยสำคัญ is the fixed Thai rendering of statistical "significant"; applied to queue time it is a calque of "substantial" and reads oddly in a systems context, where ยาวนาน/มาก is what a Thai HPC writer would use.
