editor_note: The dequantization/data-loading paragraph drops an entire balancing caveat from the English: "There are contexts in which assuming quantum data may be reasonable, but many applications of interest will start with classical data." is simply absent between "…ก็ถือว่าซ่อนเวลาที่จำเป็นสำหรับการ encoding" and "บางกรณีของ dequantization ได้แสดงให้เห็นว่า…", so the Thai teaches unqualified that assuming pre-loaded quantum data is always hiding cost. A second hedge is stripped in the "insufficient explanation" section, where "potentially interesting learning algorithms" and "naturally allows" become the flat, stronger "สิ่งนี้ทำให้เราสามารถออกแบบอัลกอริทึมการเรียนรู้ที่น่าสนใจ" — exactly the over-claim that paragraph is written to warn against. Beyond the drift, the prose carries recognizable translationese: "ความมิติสูง" (not a Thai noun; should be "การมีมิติสูง"/"มิติที่สูง") for "high dimensionality" in both the bolded takeaway and goal 2, the human pronoun "พวกเขา" used for QML types in learning goal 4, an untranslated English imperative "Implement" opening goal 5, and "entanglement" split between "พัวพันกัน" and bare English "entangled states". Terminology is otherwise sound and consistent (Qubit, superposition, feature map, kernel matrix, quantum kernel estimation left in English by a defensible convention) and the informal register holds — no ครับ/ค่ะ.

examples.source: There are contexts in which assuming quantum data may be reasonable, but many applications of interest will start with classical data.
examples.suggested: มีบางบริบทที่การสมมติว่ามีข้อมูลควอนตัมอยู่แล้วนั้นสมเหตุสมผล แต่การใช้งานที่น่าสนใจจำนวนมากจะเริ่มต้นด้วยข้อมูล classical
examples.translation: (sentence entirely absent — TH jumps from "ก็ถือว่าซ่อนเวลาที่จำเป็นสำหรับการ encoding" straight to "บางกรณีของ dequantization ได้แสดงให้เห็นว่า…")
examples.why: A whole caveat is dropped. The English deliberately concedes that assuming quantum data is sometimes legitimate before saying most real applications are not; without it the Thai reader is taught the stronger, one-sided claim that hiding encoding time is always illegitimate.

examples.source: In some cases, this naturally allows us to design potentially interesting learning algorithms based on mappings to higher dimensional spaces.
examples.suggested: ในบางกรณี สิ่งนี้ทำให้เราสามารถออกแบบอัลกอริทึมการเรียนรู้ที่อาจน่าสนใจ โดยอาศัยการ mapping ไปยังพื้นที่มิติที่สูงขึ้นได้อย่างเป็นธรรมชาติ
examples.translation: ในบางกรณี สิ่งนี้ทำให้เราสามารถออกแบบอัลกอริทึมการเรียนรู้ที่น่าสนใจตามการ mapping ไปยังพื้นที่มิติสูง
examples.why: "potentially" is dropped, turning a hedge into an assertion. This sentence is the naive story the section then dismantles as "inadequate and a bit misleading", so strengthening it blunts the whole pedagogical setup.

examples.source: For the purposes of visualizing example clusters the algorithm might identify, the data points have now been labeled.
examples.suggested: …ในภาพนี้จึงมีการติดป้ายกำกับจุดข้อมูลไว้แล้ว
examples.translation: เพื่อวัตถุประสงค์ในการแสดงภาพตัวอย่างกลุ่มที่อัลกอริทึมอาจระบุ ข้อมูลจึงได้รับการติดป้ายกำกับในที่สุด
examples.why: "ในที่สุด" (finally/eventually) makes it sound like labeling happens at the end of the algorithm, when the English means the figure shows them labeled purely for display — and the very next sentence contrasts "labeled at the end", so the two now collide.

examples.source: High dimensionality of entangled quantum states is not exponential parallelism
examples.suggested: การมีมิติสูงของสถานะควอนตัมที่พัวพันกันไม่ใช่ parallelism แบบ exponential
examples.translation: ความมิติสูงของ quantum states ที่พัวพันกันไม่ใช่ parallelism แบบ exponential
examples.why: "ความมิติสูง" is not idiomatic Thai — ความ- does not nominalize มิติ. A native writer would use "การมีมิติสูง" or "มิติที่สูง". It appears twice, including in the bolded key takeaway of the section.

examples.source: Identify different types of QML and distinguish between them.
examples.suggested: ระบุ QML ประเภทต่างๆ และแยกแยะความแตกต่างระหว่างประเภทเหล่านั้น
examples.translation: ระบุ QML ประเภทต่างๆ และแยกแยะความแตกต่างระหว่างพวกเขา
examples.why: "พวกเขา" is the animate/human pronoun; using it for categories of QML is a literal calque of English "them" that no Thai technical writer would produce.

examples.source: Implement quantum kernel methods and variational quantum classifiers using Qiskit Runtime primitives
examples.suggested: ประยุกต์ใช้ quantum kernel methods และ variational quantum classifiers โดยใช้ Qiskit Runtime primitives
examples.translation: Implement quantum kernel methods และ variational quantum classifiers โดยใช้ Qiskit Runtime primitives
examples.why: The leading verb is left untranslated while the parallel goals in the same list all start with a Thai verb (อธิบาย, ใช้, ระบุ, ปรับ). "Implement" is not a term of art that has to stay in English here — it is an untranslated leftover.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — negations ("madalas na mas kapaki-pakinabang na **huwag** ihanda at mag-sample"), all quantities (2951 Pauli terms → 1187 groups, $10^5$-$10^7$ shots, $2^{32}$ basis vectors) and the SQD upper-bound claim survive intact; domain terms are correctly kept in English (qubit, Hamiltonian, ansatz, shots, eigenvalue, wave function, subspace) with "ingay" used consistently for noise, and the register is informal (tayo/natin, no po/opo). What a native technical editor would still change: "para sa mas masikip na variance" (VQE table) calques "tighter variance" with "masikip", which in Tagalog means physically cramped/crowded — a technical writer would write "mas mahigpit" or "mas maliit na variance". "In practice, we do not need to prepare the exact ground state" becomes "Sa katotohanan, hindi natin kailangang ihanda..." — "sa katotohanan" is "in reality/in truth", not "in practice" ("sa praktika"). Two smaller drifts: "which may become infeasible to diagonalize" is strengthened to "maaaring maging imposibleng i-diagonalize" (impossible), and "the estimated ground state will be different than the exact one" becomes "iba sa eksaktong halaga" (value), shifting state→value. None of these would lead a learner to a false belief.

examples.source: **Many shots per circuit for tighter variance**.
examples.suggested: **Maraming shots bawat circuit para sa mas maliit (mas mahigpit) na variance**.
examples.translation: **Maraming shots bawat circuit para sa mas masikip na variance**.
examples.why: "Masikip" means cramped or crowded in a spatial sense; applied to a statistical variance it is a literal calque of English "tight" that no Tagalog technical writer would use. "Mas maliit" or "mas mahigpit" is the conventional rendering.

examples.source: In practice, we do not need to prepare the exact ground state as sampling many other states can give us the same set of vectors.
examples.suggested: Sa praktika, hindi natin kailangang ihanda ang eksaktong ground state...
examples.translation: Sa katotohanan, hindi natin kailangang ihanda ang eksaktong ground state dahil ang pag-sample ng maraming ibang estado ay maaaring magbigay sa atin ng parehong hanay ng mga vector.
examples.why: "Sa katotohanan" = "in truth / in reality", which reads as a factual correction rather than the English contrast between theory and practical use. The following paragraph already uses "Sa katunayan" for "In fact", so the distinction is blurred.

examples.source: A larger subspace will mean larger Hamiltonian, which may become infeasible to diagonalize.
examples.suggested: ...na maaaring hindi na maging praktikal (hindi na kayang) i-diagonalize.
examples.translation: Ang mas malaking subspace ay nangangahulugang mas malaking Hamiltonian, na maaaring maging imposibleng i-diagonalize.
examples.why: "Infeasible" (computationally impractical) is strengthened to "imposible" (impossible). The hedge "maaaring" keeps it from misleading, but the claim is stronger than the English.

examples.source: ...other computational basis states have zero amplitude in the ground state, and therefore, ideally will not appear during sampling.
examples.suggested: ...kaya sa perpektong sitwasyon ay hindi sila lalabas kapag nag-sample tayo.
examples.translation: ...kaya sa perpektong sitwasyon ay hindi sila lalabas sa panahon ng sampling.
examples.why: "Sa panahon ng sampling" is a stiff word-for-word rendering of "during sampling" (literally "in the era/period of sampling"); native technical prose would use a "kapag" clause.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, no invented claims; the dimension rules ($2^N$ by $2^M$ → M-qubit/N-qubit, the $6\times6$ non-divisible case, the `(input_dim, output_dim)` reversal caveat) all survive intact, and terminology (klase, operator, qubit, matrix, dimensyon, method/property kept in English) is consistent and correct. What a native technical editor would still change is surface polish: (1) the English-order calque "Ang `SparsePauliOp` na klase / Ang `Pauli` na klase / Ang `Operator` na klase", repeated four times, where natural Tagalog puts the head noun first ("Ang klaseng `SparsePauliOp`"); (2) a raw English finite verb dropped into a Tagalog clause in "kung ito ay (anti)commutes sa isa pang `Pauli`", which a native writer would render as "kung nag-a-(anti)commute ito"; (3) the missing ligature in "pinagbabatayan na matrix / Numpy array" (×3) — should be "pinagbabatayang". Register is correctly casual with no po/opo slips, and nothing here would mislead a learner.

examples.source: The `SparsePauliOp` class represents a linear combination of Pauli strings.
examples.suggested: Ang klaseng [`SparsePauliOp`](...) ay kumakatawan sa isang linear na kombinasyon ng mga Pauli string.
examples.translation: Ang [`SparsePauliOp`](...) na klase ay kumakatawan sa isang linear na kombinasyon ng mga Pauli string.
examples.why: "Ang X na klase" mirrors English adjective-before-noun order. Tagalog puts the head noun first with a ligature ("ang klaseng X"). Grammatical but reads as translated, and the pattern repeats for `Pauli` and `Operator`.

examples.source: ...whether it (anti)commutes with another `Pauli`...
examples.suggested: ...kung nag-a-(anti)commute ito sa isa pang `Pauli`...
examples.translation: ...kung ito ay (anti)commutes sa isa pang `Pauli`...
examples.why: An English third-person finite verb is inserted unconjugated into a Tagalog clause. Tagalog borrows English technical verbs with aspect affixes (nag-a-commute / hindi nag-a-commute); the bare "commutes" is a translationese artifact.

examples.source: The operator object stores the underlying matrix... To access the underlying Numpy array...
examples.suggested: ...ng pinagbabatayang matrix... ang pinagbabatayang Numpy array...
examples.translation: Nag-iimbak ang operator object ng pinagbabatayan na matrix... Para ma-access ang pinagbabatayan na Numpy array...
examples.why: Ligature error: a modifier ending in -n takes -g ("pinagbabatayang"), not the free particle "na". Occurs three times; a native editor would fix all three.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the hard physics is right (власні значення/власні стани, взаємно ортогональні, математичне сподівання, штрафний доданок, анзац, референсний стан), informal "ти" holds with no Ви/Вам slips. The main defect is a two-pass split in core terminology: "cost function" is "функція вартості" through the VQE/SSVQE/VQD half (lines ~41, 113, 200, 291, 371) but flips to "функція витрат" for the whole QSR section and the Summary (lines ~537, 550, 568, 593, 603); the same split hits over/under-sampling ("надвибірка та недовибірка" at line 22 vs "Надмірна вибірка / Недостатня вибірка" at 582–583) and the QSR bullet list drops from 2nd-person imperatives ("Підготуй", "Застосуй") into infinitives ("Підготувати", "Застосувати", "Виконати bootstrap" — with "bootstrap" left in English, though rendered "Виконай ініціалізацію" in the three earlier lists). Two smaller items: the English word "periodicity" is left untranslated inside Ukrainian prose ("Залежно від periodicity та смуги пропускання", line 550), and "preset pass manager" becomes "менеджера попередніх проходів" (line 158), which reads as "manager of previous passes" rather than a preconfigured pass manager. Nothing here would teach a learner a false concept — note that the line-443 "транспіляцію не вбудовано" negation contradicts the literal English but matches the code and the following sentence, so it corrects an apparent source typo rather than introducing drift.

examples.source: cost function
examples.suggested: функція вартості throughout
examples.translation: функція вартості (VQE/SSVQE/VQD sections) → функція витрат (QSR section + Summary)
examples.why: The file's single most important recurring term is rendered two different ways along a clean section boundary — a classic two-pass merge artifact; a learner reaching the QSR section may not immediately connect 'функція витрат' to the 'функція вартості' they were just taught.

examples.source: Depending on the periodicity and bandwidth of the original function
examples.suggested: Залежно від періодичності та смуги пропускання вихідної функції
examples.translation: Залежно від periodicity та смуги пропускання вихідної функції
examples.why: A bare English noun left untranslated mid-sentence, while its coordinate term 'bandwidth' was translated — an obvious leak a native editor would fix on sight.

examples.source: transpile the circuit using the preset pass manager with optimization level 3
examples.suggested: за допомогою заздалегідь налаштованого менеджера проходів (preset pass manager)
examples.translation: Транспілюємо Circuit за допомогою менеджера попередніх проходів з рівнем оптимізації 3
examples.why: 'попередніх проходів' reads as 'previous passes', mis-parsing 'preset' as 'preceding'; the Qiskit concept is a preconfigured pass manager. Recognizable from the adjacent generate_preset_pass_manager call, so imperfect rather than misleading.

examples.source: over-sampling, under-sampling
examples.suggested: Pick one pair and use it in all three places
examples.translation: надвибірка та недовибірка (intro) vs Надмірна вибірка (over-sampling) / Недостатня вибірка (under-sampling) (QSR bullets, Summary)
examples.why: The lesson intro promises two named design ideas and the Summary reprises them, but the QSR section that actually defines them uses different wording, weakening the callback structure of the lesson.

examples.source: Bootstrap at i=0 if we have a similar problem
examples.suggested: Виконай ініціалізацію при $i=0$, якщо є подібна задача
examples.translation: Виконати bootstrap при $i=0$, якщо є подібна задача
examples.why: The three earlier 'Theoretical layout' lists all use 2nd-person imperatives and translate bootstrap as 'Виконай ініціалізацію'; the QSR list switches to infinitives and leaves 'bootstrap' in English, breaking the parallel structure the four algorithm write-ups depend on.

examples.source: run our calculation on IBM Quantum hardware / If we want to run on real hardware
examples.suggested: на обладнанні IBM Quantum / на реальному обладнанні
examples.translation: запустити обчислення на залізі IBM Quantum / запустити це на реальному залізі
examples.why: 'залізо' is shop slang; the surrounding prose is otherwise standard technical Ukrainian, so the slang reads as an unmotivated drop in register for course material.

editor_note: Nothing here would actively mislead a learner — the option semantics, the min_qpy_version logic ("відхилятиме файли з версією QPY, нижчою за вказану тут") and the QISKIT_FORCE_THREADS caveat are all faithful, and informal "ти" holds throughout (ти можеш, Вкажи, Встанови, Спробуй, Ознайомся). But "circuit" is split within the file: the options section leaves it as bare capitalized English inside Ukrainian prose ("типову систему для відображення Circuit", "відображувач Circuit", "Параметри відображення Circuit"), while the environment-variables section correctly uses "схем" ("транспіляція кількох схем у Qiskit") — a native editor would unify on "схем/схеми". Second, "preset pass manager" is rendered "менеджері попередніх проходів" ("manager of previous passes"), which misparses "preset" as "pre-set/previous"; the Qiskit concept is the стандартний/попередньо налаштований менеджер проходів. Minor besides: "у старших версіях QPY" is ambiguous in software Ukrainian (reads as "higher versions" as easily as "older") where "старіших" is unambiguous, and "правилами внеску" for "contributing guidelines" is a stiff calque (настановами щодо внеску / правилами участі).

examples.source: Changes the default system for the circuit drawer. / transpilation over multiple circuits in Qiskit
examples.suggested: Змінює типову систему відображення схем. … відображувач схем шукає …
examples.translation: Змінює типову систему для відображення Circuit. … відображувач Circuit шукає JSON-таблиці стилів … / транспіляція кількох схем у Qiskit
examples.why: The core term 'circuit' is left as bare English 'Circuit' (capitalized, undeclined) in the options section and in the Admonition, but correctly translated as 'схем' in the environment-variables section — an inconsistent split of the file's most frequent domain term, and the untranslated form reads as a glossary leak rather than a deliberate keep-English choice.

examples.source: Controls the behavior of the layout and routing pass in Qiskit's preset pass manager.
examples.suggested: …у стандартному (попередньо налаштованому) менеджері проходів Qiskit.
examples.translation: Керує поведінкою проходів розміщення та маршрутизації в менеджері попередніх проходів Qiskit.
examples.why: 'preset' is misread as 'pre-set/previous' and attached to 'проходів', so the sentence names a 'manager of previous passes' — the Qiskit concept is the preset (built-in, pre-configured) pass manager. 'менеджер проходів' is still recognizable, so this is imperfect rather than misleading, but a native writer would fix the modifier.

examples.source: …when deserialization security issues are discovered in older QPY versions…
examples.suggested: …у старіших версіях QPY…
examples.translation: …у разі виявлення проблем безпеки десеріалізації у старших версіях QPY…
examples.why: In Ukrainian software prose 'старша версія' is commonly read as 'higher/newer version', which would flip the direction of the caveat relative to min_qpy_version rejecting lower versions; 'старіших' removes the ambiguity.

examples.source: Read the contributing guidelines if you want to contribute to the open-source Qiskit SDK.
examples.suggested: Ознайомся з настановами щодо внеску, якщо хочеш долучитися до розробки Qiskit SDK з відкритим кодом.
examples.translation: Ознайомся з правилами внеску, якщо хочеш зробити внесок у відкритий Qiskit SDK.
examples.why: 'правила внеску' is a word-for-word calque of 'contributing guidelines' that a Ukrainian technical writer would not produce; 'відкритий Qiskit SDK' likewise drops the sense of 'open-source' (з відкритим кодом).

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: the invitation flow, the CRN/API-key explanation and the trusted-vs-untrusted environment split are all rendered faithfully, the informal singular imperative is held consistently (اقبل، سجّل، ارجع، تأكد، اختر، جرّب), and the decision to keep "instance"/"instances" in Latin script is applied uniformly and is defensible. Three small things a native technical editor would still change: the region caveat drops one half of the English pair "see and access" (only رؤية survives, so "لن تتمكن من رؤية الـ instances..." loses the access restriction); the admonition adds an unsourced "جميع" ("lists all the instances you can access" for plain "lists the instances that you can access"); and "in the header" is calqued as the bare "في الرأس", which no Arabic technical writer would use for a page header (الشريط العلوي / رأس الصفحة). Also minor: "such as a personal laptop" becomes the stiff definite "كجهاز الحاسوب الشخصي", and the hello-world link title gains an unsourced "حقيقي" ("على عتاد حقيقي" for "on hardware").

examples.source: You can access either region by using the same API key, but you can only see and access the instances that were created in the region that you're logged in to.
examples.suggested: ... لكن لن تتمكن من رؤية الـ instances التي أُنشئت في منطقة أخرى أو الوصول إليها؛ لا ترى وتصل إلا إلى ما أُنشئ في المنطقة التي سجّلت دخولك إليها.
examples.translation: يمكنك الوصول إلى أي منطقة باستخدام نفس مفتاح API، لكن لن تتمكن من رؤية الـ instances التي أُنشئت إلا في المنطقة التي سجّلت دخولك إليها.
examples.why: The English restricts both visibility AND access; the Arabic keeps only رؤية (see) and silently drops الوصول (access). A reader could conclude the other region's instances are merely hidden but still reachable via the API key. Dropped qualifier, not a full inversion, so MINOR.

examples.source: The IBM Quantum Platform dashboard and the Instances page list the instances that you can access.
examples.suggested: تسرد ... الـ instances التي يمكنك الوصول إليها.
examples.translation: تسرد [لوحة تحكم IBM Quantum Platform] و[صفحة الـ Instances] جميع الـ instances التي يمكنك الوصول إليها.
examples.why: "جميع" (all) is not in the English and slightly strengthens the claim into a completeness guarantee about the listing. Small, non-misleading, but an editor would delete it.

examples.source: Make sure that the correct account and region are selected in the account switcher in the header, as shown in the following image.
examples.suggested: ... في أداة تبديل الحساب في الشريط العلوي (رأس الصفحة)، كما هو موضح في الصورة التالية.
examples.translation: تأكد من اختيار الحساب والمنطقة الصحيحين في أداة تبديل الحساب في الرأس، كما هو موضح في الصورة التالية.
examples.why: "في الرأس" is a bare calque of "in the header"; unqualified الرأس reads as the body part in Arabic UI prose. Native technical writing uses الشريط العلوي or رأس الصفحة. Same class as "كجهاز الحاسوب الشخصي" for "such as a personal laptop" (line 37), which is stiff and wrongly definite.

editor_note: The page's single conceptual sentence (the intro at line 33) is mistranslated in two load-bearing ways. "quasi-probability distributions" became "توزيعات احتمالية شبه كمية" — the "quasi-" modifier was transplanted from "probability" onto "كمية", so the Arabic reads "semi-quantum probability distributions", inventing a concept that does not exist and destroying the actual term (quasi-probability = the distribution that may take negative values, which is exactly what Sampler + error mitigation produces; the correct term is "توزيعات شبه احتمالية"). In the same sentence "entire error-mitigated ... distributions" became "مُخففة الأخطاء بالكامل" — "بالكامل" attaches to the nearest adjectival phrase and so asserts "fully error-mitigated", a strengthened claim the English does not make (error mitigation is never complete), while "entire" (whole distributions) and "sampled from" both disappear. Secondary, non-misleading issues: "circuit" is split within the file between Arabic "الدائرة/الدوائر" (lines 33, 125, 174) and bare English "Circuits" (line 81 and the heading at line 123), and "to return the measurement outcome" is rendered "لإعادة" (to repeat/restore) where "لإرجاع" is the correct sense.

examples.source: Generate entire error-mitigated quasi-probability distributions sampled from quantum circuit outputs.
examples.suggested: ولِّد توزيعات شبه احتمالية كاملة ومُخفَّفة الأخطاء، مأخوذة بالمعاينة من مخرجات الدوائر الكمية.
examples.translation: ولِّد توزيعات احتمالية شبه كمية مُخففة الأخطاء بالكامل من مخرجات الدائرة الكمية.
examples.why: ‘quasi-probability’ is a fixed domain term (توزيعات شبه احتمالية). Here the ‘quasi-’ was moved onto ‘كمية’, producing ‘semi-quantum probability distributions’ — a concept that does not exist and that hides the one property this page depends on (quasi-probabilities can be negative). A learner forms a false belief about what Sampler returns.

examples.source: Generate entire error-mitigated quasi-probability distributions
examples.suggested: توزيعات ... كاملة ومُخفَّفة الأخطاء
examples.translation: ... مُخففة الأخطاء بالكامل
examples.why: ‘entire’ qualifies the distributions, not the mitigation. As placed, بالكامل modifies مُخففة الأخطاء and claims the errors are *fully* mitigated — a strengthened claim the English avoids and one that is physically wrong for error mitigation. The ‘sampled from’ notion is also dropped.

examples.source: ...counts of multiple circuits in one job. / Run parameterized circuits
examples.suggested: لعدة دوائر في مهمة واحدة. / تشغيل الدوائر ذات المعاملات
examples.translation: لعدة Circuits في مهمة واحدة. / تشغيل Circuits ذات معاملات
examples.why: ‘circuit’ is rendered in Arabic (الدائرة الكمية, أداء الدائرة, إعادة استخدام الدائرة) elsewhere in the same file but left as bare English ‘Circuits’ here and in the heading — an inconsistent split of a core term within one short page.

examples.source: Use Sampler to return the measurement outcome as bitstrings or counts of a single circuit.
examples.suggested: استخدم Sampler لإرجاع نتيجة القياس على هيئة سلاسل بتات أو تعدادات لدائرة واحدة.
examples.translation: استخدم Sampler لإعادة نتيجة القياس كسلاسل بتية أو تعدادات لدائرة واحدة.
examples.why: إعادة means to repeat/restore; the API sense of ‘return a value’ is إرجاع. ‘سلاسل بتية’ is also an unusual coinage where ‘سلاسل بتات’ is the conventional rendering of bitstrings.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout (no drift found: the 30-day no-credit-card caveat, the us-east/Open Plan requirement, the "pokud jsi ... ještě neuložil" condition and the queue-time note all match the English) and the informal "ty" register holds consistently (Sestav, spusť, Zaregistruj se, můžeš). The defect is a glossary keep-English leak that a Czech technical editor would not tolerate: "circuit" is left as an undeclined, capitalized English noun everywhere ("Tvůj první kvantový Circuit", "## Sestav Circuit", "Circuit musí být nejprve transpilován", "ke spouštění Circuit") where Czech has the fully standard "kvantový obvod / obvody", and the same happens to "gate set" → "sadu Gate" instead of "sadu hradel". The file also splits its own qubit convention: lowercase Czech "qubity" in the intro but capitalized "Qubitů" in the transpilation sentence. Nothing here would make a learner form a false belief — the English words are recognizable — but "ke spouštění Circuit" and "sadu Gate" read as unedited pipeline output rather than Czech prose.

examples.source: Hello World: Your First Quantum Circuit / ## Build the circuit
examples.suggested: Hello World: Tvůj první kvantový obvod / ## Sestav obvod
examples.translation: Hello World: Tvůj první kvantový Circuit / ## Sestav Circuit
examples.why: "Kvantový obvod" is the universal Czech domain term; leaving "Circuit" as an undeclined capitalized English noun glued to a Czech adjective is a glossary keep-English leak, not a field convention (unlike qubit, which Czech genuinely borrows).

examples.source: The circuit must first be transpiled (adapted) to the device's gate set and qubit connectivity.
examples.suggested: Obvod musí být nejprve transpilován (přizpůsoben) na sadu hradel a konektivitu qubitů daného zařízení.
examples.translation: Circuit musí být nejprve transpilován (přizpůsoben) na sadu Gate a konektivitu Qubitů daného zařízení.
examples.why: "Gate" has a settled Czech equivalent, "hradlo" (sada hradel); "sadu Gate" is an untranslated, undeclined fragment. "Qubitů" is also capitalized mid-sentence, contradicting lowercase "qubity" used in the intro line.

examples.source: reference material on running circuits, primitives, and the Qiskit Runtime
examples.suggested: referenční materiály ke spouštění obvodů, primitiv a Qiskit Runtime
examples.translation: referenční materiály ke spouštění Circuit, primitiv a Qiskit Runtime
examples.why: "ke spouštění Circuit" leaves a required genitive plural unfilled — the noun cannot decline because it stayed English, so the phrase reads as broken Czech next to the correctly declined "primitiv" beside it.

examples.source: step-by-step guides on algorithms, error mitigation, transpilation, and more
examples.suggested: průvodce krok za krokem algoritmy, potlačením chyb, transpilací a dalšími tématy
examples.translation: podrobné průvodce algoritmy, potlačením chyb, transpilací a dalšími tématy
examples.why: "step-by-step" is flattened to "podrobné" (detailed), losing the sequential-walkthrough promise that distinguishes Tutorials from the Guides bullet directly below it; a dropped nuance rather than a wrong statement.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every Yes/No answer, the "whichever happens last" clause (line 77 "podle toho, co nastane jako poslední"), the five-lanes/six-jobs example (lines 122–124), and the session-vs-batch compilation-time contrast are all correct, and the informal "ty" register holds consistently (používáš, potřebuješ, zaplatíš, Chceš-li). Three things a Czech technical editor would still change: (a) "circuit" is left as bare English "Circuit" and is not declined in the plural — "všechny Circuit spuštěny" (l.97) and "Všechny tvé Circuit poběží dohromady" (l.106) are ungrammatical, while l.108 does decline it ("příliš mnoho Circuitů ... jsou Circuit příliš velké"), so the same term is handled two ways in one bullet list; standard Czech usage is "obvod"/"kvantový obvod". (b) "wall clock time" is calqued as "čas nástěnných hodin" (l.77, l.115) — a literal rendering no Czech engineer writes; "reálný uplynulý čas" or "čas podle reálných hodin" is the idiom. (c) a spelling error, "nezískaš" for "nezískáš" (l.107), plus a mismatched closing quote in „prováděcí dráhy" (l.120). None of these mislead a learner.

examples.source: ...when all circuits are executed in a single job. / All of your circuits will run together. / if it contains too many circuits or if the circuits are too large.
examples.suggested: ...kdy jsou všechny obvody spuštěny v rámci jediné úlohy. / Všechny tvé obvody poběží dohromady. / pokud obsahuje příliš mnoho obvodů nebo pokud jsou obvody příliš velké.
examples.translation: ...kdy jsou všechny Circuit spuštěny v rámci jediné úlohy. / Všechny tvé Circuit poběží dohromady. / pokud obsahuje příliš mnoho Circuitů nebo pokud jsou Circuit příliš velké.
examples.why: 'Circuit' is kept in English and left undeclined, producing ungrammatical Czech ('všechny Circuit spuštěny'), and it is handled inconsistently within three adjacent bullets (bare 'Circuit' vs. declined 'Circuitů'). Czech quantum writing uses 'obvod' / 'kvantový obvod'.

examples.source: usage is the wall clock time the QPU is committed to the session / when a batch's wall clock time ... exceeds the system-defined maximum time
examples.suggested: je využití reálný uplynulý čas, po který je QPU přiděleno Session / když reálný uplynulý čas dávky ... překročí systémem definovaný maximální čas
examples.translation: je využití čas nástěnných hodin, po který je QPU přiděleno Session / když čas nástěnných hodin dávky ... překročí systémem definovaný maximální čas
examples.why: 'čas nástěnných hodin' is a word-for-word calque of 'wall clock time'; a native technical writer says 'reálný uplynulý čas' or 'skutečně uplynulý čas'. Meaning survives, but it reads as machine translation.

examples.source: If this single job fails, you don't get partial results.
examples.suggested: Pokud tato jediná úloha selže, nezískáš částečné výsledky.
examples.translation: Pokud tato jediná úloha selže, nezískaš částečné výsledky.
examples.why: Spelling error: the 2nd-person singular ending requires a long vowel, 'nezískáš'. The informal register itself is correct and consistent with the rest of the file.

examples.source: when the first job in your batch starts running
examples.suggested: Jakmile však první úloha z tvé dávky začne běžet
examples.translation: Jakmile se však první úloha z tvé dávky začne spouštět
examples.why: 'začne spouštět' shifts to the launching process rather than the job actually running; 'začne běžet' matches 'starts running' and is what a Czech engineer would write.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner — the meaning, the numbers (156 Qubits, -242.0, kubisch/quadratisch/linear), the "niedrigere Werte = bessere Lösungen" logic and the consistent "du"-Register are all faithful — but a native technical editor would still change several things. "utility scale" is rendered two ways in the same file ("im Utility-Maßstab", line 28, vs. "dieses Utility-Scale-Problems", line 545), and circuits are left in English ("die Ausführung der Quantum Circuits", line 480) while everything around them is Germanized (Quantenhardware, Quantenalgorithmus, Quantenausführung) — "Quantenschaltkreise" is the term the rest of the file's register calls for. Two qualifiers thin out: the frontmatter compound "ein quantenoptimiertes Problem im Utility-Maßstab" (line 4) says "quantum-optimized problem" rather than EN's "quantum optimization problem", and "random-bond ... Ising model" loses the bond disorder as plain "eines zufälligen 156-Qubit-Ising-Modells" (line 26); line 82 likewise drops "the construction of" from "der Problemdefinition". Finally line 546 carries two calques a German writer would not produce: the coinage "Klassiklösung" (should be "klassische Lösung") and "konsistent niedrigere Kosten" for "consistently" (durchgängig/durchweg).

examples.source: it achieves accurate solutions at utility scale / The complexity of this utility-scale problem
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering and keep it — e.g. "im Utility-Maßstab" and "dieses Problems im Utility-Maßstab".
examples.translation: genaue Lösungen im Utility-Maßstab / Die Komplexität dieses Utility-Scale-Problems
examples.why: The same concept is rendered two different ways within one short file; a reader may not connect the two mentions.

examples.source: running the quantum circuits with error suppression
examples.suggested: die Ausführung der Quantenschaltkreise mit Fehlerunterdrückung
examples.translation: die Ausführung der Quantum Circuits mit Fehlerunterdrückung
examples.why: The file otherwise Germanizes every quantum compound (Quantenhardware, Quantenalgorithmus, Quantenausführung, Quantum-free "Grundzustandsenergie"); leaving only "Quantum Circuits" in English is an inconsistent register slip, not a settled English-keeps convention.

examples.source: the ground-state energy of a random-bond 156-qubit Ising model possessing cubic terms
examples.suggested: ... eines 156-Qubit-Ising-Modells mit zufälligen Kopplungen (random-bond) und kubischen Termen
examples.translation: die Grundzustandsenergie eines zufälligen 156-Qubit-Ising-Modells mit kubischen Termen
examples.why: "random-bond" is a specific model class (disorder in the couplings); "zufälliges Ising-Modell" reads as a vaguely random model and loses where the randomness lives.

examples.source: a distribution of randomly sampled bitstrings, which is equivalent to a "brute-force" classical solution. If the algorithm consistently finds lower costs
examples.suggested: ... die einer klassischen „Brute-Force"-Lösung entspricht. Wenn der Algorithmus durchgängig niedrigere Kosten findet
examples.translation: einer Verteilung zufällig gesampelter Bitstrings, die einer „Brute-Force"-Klassiklösung entspricht. Wenn der Algorithmus konsistent niedrigere Kosten findet
examples.why: "Klassiklösung" is an invented compound no German technical writer would use, and "konsistent" is a false-friend calque of "consistently" (German "konsistent" means internally coherent, not repeatedly).

examples.source: Solve a utility-scale quantum optimization problem ... fully automates the hardware-aware implementation steps
examples.suggested: Löse ein Quantenoptimierungsproblem im Utility-Maßstab ... automatisiert vollständig die hardwarenahen Implementierungsschritte
examples.translation: Löse ein quantenoptimiertes Problem im Utility-Maßstab ... automatisiert vollständig die hardware-bewussten Implementierungsschritte
examples.why: "quantenoptimiertes Problem" inverts the compound (quantum-optimized problem instead of quantum optimization problem), and "hardware-bewusst" is a literal calque of "hardware-aware"; "hardwarenah"/"hardwarespezifisch" is what a German engineer writes.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no dropped caveats (the Open-Plan session restriction, the "not all of it" open-source qualifier and the non-open-source service software are all intact), and "du" holds consistently. What a native editor would still change: (1) "readout mitigation" is rendered "Ausleseminderung", a coinage that literally says "reduction of readout" rather than mitigation of readout *errors* — recognizable in the error-mitigation list, but "Readout-Mitigation" or "Minderung von Auslesefehlern" is the conventional rendering; likewise "dynamical decoupling" → "dynamisches Entkoppeln" instead of the standard "dynamische Entkopplung". (2) In the IBM Quantum Platform paragraph, "permissions" and "entitlements" collapse into the same word, yielding the redundant "Berechtigungen verwalten, Berechtigungen konfigurieren" and flattening the admin/billing distinction the English draws. (3) "deploy" is split within the file — "Deployment von Programmen" in the Serverless intro vs. "bereitzustellen" in the bullet — and "persist long-running workloads" becomes "speichern", which reads as archiving rather than keeping them alive. (4) Some noun-stack calques ("Algorithmusentdeckung und das Anwendungsprototyping", "domänenvertrauten Eingaben und Ausgaben", "Messungs-Observablen") are stiffer than a German technical writer would produce.

examples.source: Examples include dynamical decoupling for error suppression, and readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) for error mitigation.
examples.suggested: Beispiele hierfür sind dynamische Entkopplung zur Fehlerunterdrückung sowie Readout-Mitigation (Minderung von Auslesefehlern) und Zero-Noise-Extrapolation (ZNE) zur Fehlerminderung.
examples.translation: Beispiele hierfür sind dynamisches Entkoppeln zur Fehlerunterdrückung sowie Ausleseminderung und Zero-Noise-Extrapolation (ZNE) zur Fehlerminderung.
examples.why: "Ausleseminderung" literally reads as "reducing the readout", not mitigating readout *errors*; "dynamisches Entkoppeln" uses a verbal noun where the field's fixed term is "dynamische Entkopplung". Recognizable in context, so minor, but neither is the established German term.

examples.source: Administrators can manage memberships and permissions, configure entitlements, and oversee usage
examples.suggested: Administratoren können Mitgliedschaften und Zugriffsrechte verwalten, Nutzungskontingente konfigurieren und die Nutzung überwachen
examples.translation: Administratoren können Mitgliedschaften und Berechtigungen verwalten, Berechtigungen konfigurieren und die Nutzung überwachen
examples.why: "permissions" and "entitlements" both become "Berechtigungen", so the sentence repeats itself and loses the English distinction between access rights and allocated usage entitlements.

examples.source: This includes deploying programs to IBM Quantum Platform … / Deploy reusable programs in the cloud
examples.suggested: Use one rendering throughout, e.g. "das Bereitstellen von Programmen auf IBM Quantum Platform" … "Wiederverwendbare Programme in der Cloud bereitzustellen"
examples.translation: Dazu gehören das Deployment von Programmen auf IBM Quantum Platform … / Wiederverwendbare Programme in der Cloud bereitzustellen
examples.why: The same operation (deploy) is rendered two ways within four lines; a learner may read "Deployment" and "bereitstellen" as two different capabilities of Qiskit Serverless.

examples.source: Persist long-running workloads in the cloud, even if your laptop is turned off / accelerate algorithm discovery and application prototyping
examples.suggested: Lang laufende Workloads in der Cloud weiterlaufen zu lassen, auch wenn dein Laptop ausgeschaltet ist / die Suche nach Algorithmen und das Prototyping von Anwendungen zu beschleunigen
examples.translation: Lang laufende Workloads in der Cloud zu speichern, auch wenn dein Laptop ausgeschaltet ist / die Algorithmusentdeckung und das Anwendungsprototyping zu beschleunigen
examples.why: "speichern" suggests archiving a finished workload rather than keeping a running one alive, which weakens the point of the bullet; "Algorithmusentdeckung"/"Anwendungsprototyping" are noun-stack calques a German technical writer would unpack.

editor_note: Nothing misleading: the technical content is faithful throughout — 156 qubits, the 1-to-1 variable↔qubit mapping, "no variacional", the ~10 vs ~100 iteration comparison, the AR formula gloss, and the "establece `direct_qubit_mapping` en `True`" instruction all match the English exactly, terminology is correct and consistent (qubit, puertas de entrelazamiento, estado fundamental, función objetivo, campo de sesgo/bias-field, posprocesamiento, transpilador, shots/backend/solver kept in English), and the informal tú register holds without a single usted slip (Consulta, Ten en cuenta, Autentícate, Prueba). What a native editor would still change is a handful of calqued/clumsy phrasings: "El algoritmo ejecuta varias iteraciones de ejecuciones en hardware" repeats the ejecutar root twice in five words; "donde trabajamos todo el proceso de usar Iskay Solver" is a literal calque of "work through the whole process" that no Spanish technical writer would produce; and "para entregar automáticamente las soluciones a los problemas" calques "deliver" where "proporcionar/obtener" is the idiom. Also mildly stiff, though defensible: "Típicamente, aproximadamente diez iteraciones son suficientes" stacks two adverbs where "Por lo general, unas diez iteraciones bastan" reads native.

examples.source: The algorithm executes several iterations of hardware runs to obtain the final solutions and combines it with post-processing.
examples.suggested: El algoritmo realiza varias iteraciones de ejecución en hardware para obtener las soluciones finales y las combina con posprocesamiento.
examples.translation: El algoritmo ejecuta varias iteraciones de ejecuciones en hardware para obtener las soluciones finales y las combina con posprocesamiento.
examples.why: "ejecuta varias iteraciones de ejecuciones" repeats the ejecutar root twice in the same clause and stacks two plurals (iteraciones de ejecuciones); a native writer would use realiza/lleva a cabo and singular "ejecución en hardware". Meaning is intact, only the prose is clumsy.

examples.source: where we work through the whole process of using Iskay Solver to address the Market Split problem
examples.suggested: donde recorremos paso a paso todo el proceso de uso de Iskay Solver para abordar el problema Market Split
examples.translation: donde trabajamos todo el proceso de usar Iskay Solver para abordar el problema Market Split
examples.why: "trabajamos todo el proceso" is a word-for-word calque of English "work through"; in Spanish trabajar does not take a process as direct object this way. Recorrer/repasar paso a paso is the idiomatic rendering in tutorial prose.

examples.source: requiring only the objective function as input to automatically deliver problem solutions
examples.suggested: que solo necesita la función objetivo como entrada para proporcionar automáticamente las soluciones del problema
examples.translation: que requiere únicamente la función objetivo como entrada para entregar automáticamente las soluciones a los problemas
examples.why: "entregar ... las soluciones a los problemas" calques "deliver problem solutions"; entregar reads as physical delivery here, and "las soluciones a los problemas" is a wordy expansion of the English compound. Proporcionar/devolver las soluciones del problema is the conventional phrasing.

editor_note: Faithful and idiomatic throughout, with no semantic drift: the authentication caveat ("El servidor MCP de Qiskit y el servidor MCP de Qiskit Docs no requieren autenticación") keeps the exact scope of the English, and terminology is correct and consistent (backends left in English, transpilar/transpilación, jobs→trabajos, reinforcement learning→aprendizaje por refuerzo, "pases de transpilador potenciados por IA" matching the corpus convention); informal tú holds everywhere ("Instala", "Puedes probar", "Consulta la documentación de tu cliente MCP", "te ayuden").

Meaning is faithful throughout — the "smaller of the two values" direction, the 5000 s / ~83 min vs 300 s example, the "running jobs continue, queued jobs go to a failed state" split, and the non-configurable interactive-TTL caveat all survive intact, and the informal register (tu / Définis / Consulte) is consistent. Two wordings a native technical editor would still change: "wall clock time" is rendered « le temps réel » (line 25), which in French primarily evokes *temps réel* = real-time computing rather than elapsed clock time — « le temps écoulé » or « le temps d'horloge » is the domain wording; and "fair device usage" becomes « utilisation équitable des appareils » (line 51), where « appareils » reads consumer-appliance rather than QPU hardware (« dispositifs » or « ressources » is the idiomatic choice). Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent, with job/batch/session/TTL/timeout/QPU/Estimator/Sampler/Executor sensibly kept in English. Nothing here would mislead a learner.

examples.source: The `max_execution_time` value is based on *QPU usage*, not wall clock time.
examples.suggested: La valeur `max_execution_time` est basée sur *l'utilisation du QPU*, et non sur le temps écoulé (temps d'horloge).
examples.translation: La valeur `max_execution_time` est basée sur *l'utilisation du QPU*, et non sur le temps réel.
examples.why: « temps réel » is the standard French term for real-time computing; used here for 'wall clock time' it is recognizable from context but is not the domain rendering a French engineer would write.

examples.source: This service-calculated timeout is capped at 3 hours to ensure fair device usage.
examples.suggested: … pour garantir une utilisation équitable des dispositifs (ou : des ressources quantiques).
examples.translation: Ce timeout calculé par le service est plafonné à 3 heures pour garantir une utilisation équitable des appareils.
examples.why: « appareils » carries a consumer-appliance connotation in French; for QPU hardware a native technical writer would use « dispositifs » or « ressources ».

examples.source: You can also find how much usage completed jobs have consumed by returning the job metrics as follows:
examples.suggested: Tu peux aussi savoir quelle utilisation les jobs terminés ont consommée en récupérant les métriques du job, comme suit :
examples.translation: Tu peux aussi connaître l'utilisation consommée par les jobs terminés en récupérant les métriques du job comme suit :
examples.why: « l'utilisation consommée » is a slightly redundant calque of 'how much usage … have consumed'; defensible and clear, noted only as stiffness, not a defect on its own.

editor_note: Faithful and idiomatic: the noise-management intro keeps the full trade-off ("trouver un équilibre entre perfectionner tes résultats et faire en sorte que ton job se termine dans un délai raisonnable"), core terms follow French Qiskit convention and stay consistent (dynamical decoupling → découplage dynamique, Pauli twirling → twirling de Pauli, error mitigation/suppression → atténuation et suppression d'erreurs, Sampler/backend/job left in English), and the informal tu register holds throughout (Consulte, Décide, tes, ton).

Meaning is faithful throughout — dates (2026, 2029, 2033+), the two quantum-advantage criteria, "millions of gates / thousands of logical qubits", and the "not replacement but integration" framing all survive intact, and the mixed-script glossary (Circuitים / Qubitים / Gateים / QPUים) is applied consistently, so nothing here would actually mislead a learner. What a native technical editor would change: "co-processors" is rendered "מעבדים משותפים" (= *shared* processors) instead of "מעבדי עזר"/"מעבדים נלווים"; "classical diagonalization" is "אלכסון קלאסי" (= diagonal, the line) rather than the standard Hebrew "לכסון קלאסי" — awkward in a course built on SQD/SKQD; and "reproduced" becomes "ייועתקו" (= copied) even though the Summary correctly uses "שחזוריות" for reproducibility. "Fault tolerance" is split within the file between the heading "סובלנות לתקלות" (social tolerance) and the body's correct "עמידות בפני תקלות", and in the FTQC bullet the relative pronoun "שהוא" after "מרעש" grammatically attaches the "critical element in achieving fault tolerance" claim to *noise* rather than to error mitigation. Add scattered calques and stiffness ("ההנעה שביסוד השימוש" for motivation, "זרמי עבודה" for workflows, "ערימות תוכנה" for software stacks, "לפרלול" for parallelize, "בקנה מידה" left dangling for "at scale") plus two agreement slips ("עד שתושג קונסנסוס", "הרעיונות המפתח").

examples.source: QPUs are envisioned as specialized co-processors, working alongside CPUs and GPUs
examples.suggested: QPUים מתוארים כמעבדי עזר ייעודיים, הפועלים לצד CPUים ו-GPUים
examples.translation: QPUים מתוארים כמעבדים משותפים מיוחדים, הפועלים לצד CPUים ו-GPUים
examples.why: ‘מעבד משותף’ means a *shared* processor (multi-tenant), a different concept from a co-processor. The adjacent ‘הפועלים לצד’ lets the reader recover the intent, so it is recognizable rather than misleading, but it is the wrong term.

examples.source: quantum states, which define a subspace for classical diagonalization
examples.suggested: מצבים קוונטיים המגדירים תת-מרחב ללכסון קלאסי
examples.translation: מצבים קוונטיים המגדירים תת-מרחב לאלכסון קלאסי
examples.why: In Hebrew ‘אלכסון’ is the diagonal (the line); the process of diagonalizing a matrix is ‘לכסון’. In a lesson whose whole payload is Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization the process noun is the one that matters.

examples.source: a sequence of increasingly robust demonstrations that will be scrutinized, reproduced, and challenged by the community
examples.suggested: רצף של הדגמות הולכות ומתחזקות שייבחנו, ישוחזרו ויאותגרו על ידי הקהילה
examples.translation: רצף של הדגמות הולכות ומתחזקות שייבחנו, ייועתקו ויאותגרו על ידי הקהילה
examples.why: ‘ייועתקו’ = will be copied/duplicated, not scientific replication. It also contradicts the Summary, which correctly renders reproducibility as ‘שחזוריות’ — the same concept, two words, one of them wrong.

examples.source: error mitigation uses classical post-processing to reduce or eliminate the bias in calculations caused by noise, which is also a critical element in achieving system-level fault-tolerant quantum systems
examples.suggested: …את ההטיה בחישובים הנגרמת מרעש; הפחתת השגיאות היא גם אלמנט קריטי בהשגת מערכות קוונטיות עמידות בפני תקלות ברמת המערכת
examples.translation: הפחתת שגיאות משתמשת בעיבוד קלאסי לאחר מעשה כדי להפחית או לבטל את ההטיה בחישובים הנגרמת מרעש, שהוא גם אלמנט קריטי בהשגת מערכות קוונטיות עמידות בפני תקלות ברמת המערכת
examples.why: The masculine ‘שהוא’ lands on the nearest masculine noun, ‘רעש’ (noise), so the sentence literally credits *noise* with being a critical element of fault tolerance. Repeating the subject removes the mis-attachment.

examples.source: System-level fault-tolerance … fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC)
examples.suggested: עמידות בפני תקלות ברמת המערכת … מחשוב קוונטי עמיד בפני תקלות (FTQC)
examples.translation: סובלנות לתקלות ברמת המערכת … מחשוב קוונטי עמיד בפני תקלות (FTQC)
examples.why: The bullet heading uses ‘סובלנות’ (tolerance in the social sense) while the body of the same bullet, and lines 55 and later, consistently use ‘עמידות בפני תקלות’. Align the heading to the body.

examples.source: motivation … workflows … parallelize … software stacks … at scale
examples.suggested: המוטיבציה / המניע … תהליכי עבודה … למיקבול … מחסניות תוכנה (או: stacks תוכנה) … בקנה מידה גדול
examples.translation: ההנעה שביסוד השימוש … זרמי עבודה … לפרלול … ערימות תוכנה … בקנה מידה
examples.why: ‘ההנעה’ is propulsion, ‘זרמי עבודה’ and ‘ערימות תוכנה’ are word-for-word calques (a CS stack is ‘מחסנית’, not ‘ערימה’), ‘פרלול’ is invented where ‘מיקבול’ is standard, and ‘בקנה מידה’ without ‘גדול’ dangles. Individually small, together they give the page a machine-translated texture a Hebrew engineer would not write.

examples.source: details the key ideas ahead … until a scientific consensus is reached
examples.suggested: מפרט את רעיונות המפתח שלפנינו … עד שיושג קונסנסוס מדעי
examples.translation: מפרט את הרעיונות המפתח שלפנינו … עד שתושג קונסנסוס מדעי
examples.why: Two agreement slips: ‘הרעיונות המפתח’ mis-forms the construct state (should be ‘רעיונות המפתח’), and ‘קונסנסוס’ is masculine so the verb must be ‘יושג’, not ‘תושג’.

examples.source: Once the curves cross, the space between them corresponds to quantum advantage.
examples.suggested: ברגע שהעקומות נחתכות, המרחב ביניהן מייצג את היתרון הקוונטי.
examples.translation: ברגע שהעקומות נחצות, המרחב ביניהן מתאים ליתרון קוונטי.
examples.why: ‘נחצות’ means bisected/crossed-over by something else; two curves crossing each other are ‘נחתכות’/‘מצטלבות’. ‘מתאים ל’ also under-translates ‘corresponds to’ in this figure caption.

editor_note: FAIL is driven by one factual mis-teaching: the "extended Euclidean algorithm" is rendered "אלגוריתם אויילר המורחב" (extended EULER algorithm) at HE lines 190 and 319, and its tooltip repeats it ("משפר על אלגוריתם אויילר המקורי"). This sits two lines below "הטוטיינט של אויילר" (Euler's totient), so the learner is actively led to believe the modular-inverse algorithm is Euler's; the same algorithm is then correctly called "אלגוריתם אוקלידס המורחב" at line 732, so the file contradicts itself. Beyond that, the file reads as a two-pass merge: from line 686 to the end, 42 DefinitionTooltip `definition` attributes are left in raw English while the first half's are Hebrew, and core terms split across the seam — non-repudiation is אי-כפירה (28/41/74) then אי-הכחשה (543/681/683), KEM is מנגנון אנקפסולציה של מפתח (67/373) then מנגנון עטיפת מפתח (449/450), plain text is טקסט פשוט then טקסט גלוי/טקסט רגיל, modular inverse is היפוך כפלי then הופכי כפלי, and Alice/Bob appear as אליס/בוב in the RSA sections but as Latin "Alice"/"Bob" throughout the Diffie-Hellman accordions (903–983). Smaller native-editor items: a function's *period* is "תקופה"/"תקופתית" (an era) instead of מחזור/מחזורית (760, 775, 818, 869, 881); "computers" is "קומפיוטרים" at 22/137 but "מחשבים" everywhere else; "scaling" is transliterated "סקאלביליות" (696, 706, 822); "Facet 1" becomes "פאסט 1" (1432); plus grammar slips (הוא אחת מהקריפטוסיסטמות 154, בלכל היותר 1428, זוהי תהליך 1434, לאיזשהו קבוצה 1405).

examples.source: This is more efficiently computed using the extended Euclidean algorithm. / ... the computationally efficient extended Euclidean algorithm is used for this purpose.
examples.suggested: אלגוריתם אוקלידס המורחב (tooltip: "משפר על אלגוריתם אוקלידס המקורי")
examples.translation: חישוב זה יעיל יותר באמצעות אלגוריתם אויילר המורחב. (tooltip: "משפר על אלגוריתם אויילר המקורי") / ... אלגוריתם אויילר המורחב היעיל חישובית משמש למטרה זו.
examples.why: Euclid is replaced by Euler — a false attribution taught twice plus in the tooltip, immediately after 'הטוטיינט של אויילר' in the same section, so the learner will merge the two. Line 732 renders the very same algorithm correctly as 'אלגוריתם אוקלידס המורחב', leaving the file self-contradictory. This is the FAIL.

examples.source: When used for encryption, it yields ciphertext that is inscrutable, and without access to the private key, inverting the operation ... is not feasible.
examples.suggested: היא מניבה טקסט מוצפן בלתי-מובן (as at line 120), וללא גישה למפתח הפרטי ...
examples.translation: כאשר משתמשים בה להצפנה, היא מניבה טקסט מוצפן שאינו ניתן לפענוח, וללא גישה למפתח הפרטי, היפוך הפעולה ... אינו אפשרי.
examples.why: 'inscrutable' is strengthened to 'that cannot be decrypted', which contradicts the end of the same sentence ('עם גישה למפתח הפרטי ... ניתן לפענח בקלות') and the trapdoor idea being taught. Line 120 already renders inscrutable correctly as 'בלתי-מובן'.

examples.source: <DefinitionTooltip definition="A quantum algorithm which can find prime factors efficiently...">Shor's algorithm</DefinitionTooltip>
examples.suggested: אלגוריתם קוונטי שמוצא גורמים ראשוניים ביעילות. פותח על ידי המתמטיקאי פיטר שור ב-1994.
examples.translation: <DefinitionTooltip definition="A quantum algorithm which can find prime factors efficiently...">האלגוריתם של שור</DefinitionTooltip>
examples.why: From 'שבירת RSA' onward every glossary definition the reader hovers is untranslated English, while the first half's 52 tooltips are Hebrew. The teaching aid silently stops working in Hebrew exactly where the material gets hardest.

examples.source: find the period r such that 6^r ≡ 1 (mod 247) / step 2 is the crucial period-finding operation / periodic with period p-1
examples.suggested: למצוא את המחזור $r$ ... / פעולת מציאת המחזור המכרעת ... / היא מחזורית עם מחזור $p-1$
examples.translation: למצוא את התקופה $r$ ... / פעולת מציאת התקופה המכרעת ... / היא תקופתית עם תקופה $p-1$
examples.why: 'תקופה' is a span of time/era; the mathematical period of a function is 'מחזור'. Line 869 even mixes both in one sentence ('המחזור חוזר ... עם תקופה $p-1$'), and 'חבורה מחזורית' is used correctly elsewhere, so the reader meets two words for one concept.

examples.source: The private key is a randomly chosen integer $d$ with as many bits as in the prime $p$.
examples.suggested: המפתח הפרטי הוא מספר שלם $d$ שנבחר באקראי, במספר סיביות זהה לזה של הראשוני $p$.
examples.translation: המפתח הפרטי הוא מספר שלם $d$ שנבחר באקראי עם כמה סיביות כמו בראשוני $p$.
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of 'as many bits as'; in Hebrew 'עם כמה סיביות' reads as 'with a few bits', losing the equal-length requirement that gives the key its security.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every plan, limit and condition matches the English (10 menit per jendela 28 hari, minimal 400 menit, lebih dari 10.000 menit → Premium, us-east only), the "kamu" informal register holds throughout, and plan names/UI labels (Open Plan, Flex Plan, Platform dashboard, Workloads) are correctly left untranslated. Two things a native technical editor would change: (1) "circuit" is left in English AND capitalized mid-sentence three times — "Jalankan Circuit kuantummu", "Jalankan Circuit kuantum" (×2) — which reads as a glossary keep-English substitution artifact; Indonesian technical prose writes "sirkuit kuantum" (lowercase) or at minimum lowercase "circuit kuantum", since Indonesian does not capitalize common nouns mid-sentence. (2) "28-day rolling window" is calqued as "jendela bergulir 28 hari", a literal rendering no Indonesian cloud/quantum doc would use; the idiomatic phrasing is "periode bergulir 28 hari" or "dalam setiap periode 28 hari". Neither misleads a learner.

examples.source: Run your quantum circuits on the world's best QPUs for free
examples.suggested: Jalankan sirkuit kuantummu di QPU terbaik di dunia secara gratis
examples.translation: Jalankan Circuit kuantummu di QPU terbaik di dunia secara gratis
examples.why: "Circuit" is kept in English and capitalized mid-sentence in all three plan intros (Open, Pay-As-You-Go, Premium). Indonesian does not capitalize common nouns mid-sentence, so this reads as an automated glossary substitution rather than authored prose; the conventional domain term is "sirkuit kuantum".

examples.source: for free (up to 10 minutes per 28-day rolling window)
examples.suggested: secara gratis (hingga 10 menit per periode bergulir 28 hari)
examples.translation: secara gratis (hingga 10 menit per jendela bergulir 28 hari)
examples.why: "jendela bergulir" is a word-for-word calque of "rolling window". The quantity and meaning survive, but an Indonesian technical writer would say "periode bergulir 28 hari" or "dalam setiap periode 28 hari"; "jendela" for a time interval is translationese.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — nothing here would mislead a learner: the approximation_degree polarity (1.0 = tidak ada aproksimasi, 0.0 = aproksimasi maksimal), the backend/target override logic, the asap/alap descriptions and the "Transpiler tidak akan mengubah apa pun yang kamu tentukan secara manual" caveat all match the English, and the informal "kamu" register is consistent. What a native technical editor would still change: (a) generic terms are capitalized as if proper nouns mid-sentence — "Transpiler", "Backend" everywhere (lines 33, 39, 90, 105–107, 127, 163) and "Circuit kuantum" in the frontmatter description vs lowercase "circuit abstrak" in the body, so the same term is rendered two ways in one file; (b) "permute qubits through swaps" is flattened to "memindahkan qubit melalui swap" ("move" rather than "permute"); (c) the hedge in "should only be necessary" is dropped in "Menerapkan konfigurasi kustom hanya diperlukan ketika…", which reads as a firm rule rather than a rule of thumb; (d) "at the expense of" rendered as "dengan imbalan" (imbalan = reward) is an odd collocation for a trade-off.

examples.source: The transpiler's function is to change arbitrary circuits… / quantum circuit transpilation
examples.suggested: lowercase the generic nouns: "Fungsi transpiler adalah…", "opsi backend lainnya", and "transpilasi circuit kuantum" in the description so "circuit" is rendered the same way everywhere
examples.translation: Fungsi Transpiler adalah mengubah circuit sembarang… / transpilasi Circuit kuantum (frontmatter description)
examples.why: "Transpiler", "Backend" and "Circuit" are capitalized mid-sentence as if proper nouns; Indonesian technical prose keeps borrowed common nouns lowercase, and the description/body split makes "circuit" inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: The final layout is not guaranteed to be the same, as the transpiler might permute qubits through swaps or other means.
examples.suggested: …karena transpiler bisa mempermutasi (menukar posisi) qubit melalui swap atau cara lain.
examples.translation: Layout akhir tidak dijamin sama, karena Transpiler bisa memindahkan qubit melalui swap atau cara lain.
examples.why: "memindahkan" means "move"; the English point is specifically permutation of the qubit assignment, which is what makes the final layout differ from the initial one.

examples.source: Applying a custom configuration should only be necessary when a unitary synthesis plugin is specified with the `unitary_synthesis` argument.
examples.suggested: Menerapkan konfigurasi kustom seharusnya hanya diperlukan ketika plugin sintesis unitary ditentukan dengan argumen `unitary_synthesis`.
examples.translation: Menerapkan konfigurasi kustom hanya diperlukan ketika plugin sintesis unitary ditentukan dengan argumen `unitary_synthesis`.
examples.why: The English hedge "should only be necessary" is dropped, turning a rule of thumb into a categorical statement — a strengthened claim, though not one that misleads about behavior.

examples.source: Higher levels generate more optimized circuits, at the expense of longer transpilation time.
examples.suggested: …, dengan konsekuensi waktu transpilasi yang lebih lama.
examples.translation: Level yang lebih tinggi menghasilkan circuit yang lebih optimal, dengan imbalan waktu transpilasi yang lebih lama.
examples.why: "imbalan" carries the sense of a reward/compensation; for a cost trade-off a native technical writer would use "dengan konsekuensi" or "dengan biaya".

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — I checked every factual row of the timeline (1.121/1.386+/4.000 qubit, 433-qubit Osprey, Heron 133→156 qubit, "la metà del tasso di errore di gate") and every claim, negation and caveat survives intact; the translator even repaired two defects in the English source (the run-on "Eagle answers more accurate…" becomes the correct "Eagle ha fornito risposte più accurate rispetto ai metodi di approssimazione classica", and the mangled "1018 identical molecules" is correctly restored as 10<sup>18</sup>). Informal "tu" holds without a slip ("avrai", "Considera", "consulta", "clicca", "Tieni a mente"). What a native technical editor would still change is a handful of English-shaped constructions: "hardware e software informati dall'esperienza specifica del dominio" ("informed by" calqued as "informati da", and *expertise* weakened to "esperienza" rather than "competenze"); "chiuse famosamente il suo discorso inaugurale" (the English adverbial "famously" transplanted whole, plus "keynote" narrowed to "inaugurale"); "i principali motori di questa prossima generazione di calcolo" for *major drivers*; and the trailing adjective pile-up "il controllo a due qubit e a singolo qubit rapido e ad alta fedeltà". There is also a mild within-file split on "computing", rendered variously as "computing" (kept), "calcolo", "computazionale" and "informatica" — recognizable everywhere, but not a single convention.

examples.source: physicists and engineers can create hardware and software informed by domain-specific expertise
examples.suggested: fisici e ingegneri possono creare hardware e software basati su competenze specifiche di dominio
examples.translation: fisici e ingegneri possono creare hardware e software informati dall'esperienza specifica del dominio
examples.why: "informati da" is a direct calque of "informed by" — in Italian "informare" does not carry the sense of "shaped/guided by"; and "expertise" is flattened to "esperienza" where "competenze" is the domain term. Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: he famously closed his keynote speech with the statement
examples.suggested: concluse il suo intervento con la celebre frase
examples.translation: chiuse famosamente il suo discorso inaugurale con la frase
examples.why: "chiuse famosamente" transplants the English sentence adverb; Italian moves the emphasis onto the noun ("la celebre frase"). "discorso inaugurale" also narrows "keynote" to an opening address.

examples.source: outlines major drivers for this next generation of computing
examples.suggested: delinea i principali fattori trainanti di questa prossima generazione di computing
examples.translation: delinea i principali motori di questa prossima generazione di calcolo
examples.why: "motori" is a literal rendering of "drivers"; Italian business prose uses "fattori trainanti" or keeps "driver". Also one of the four different renderings of "computing" in the file (computing / calcolo / computazionale / informatica).

examples.source: The signals required to enable the fast, high-fidelity two-qubit and single-qubit control
examples.suggested: I segnali necessari per il controllo rapido e ad alta fedeltà a due qubit e a singolo qubit
examples.translation: I segnali necessari per abilitare il controllo a due qubit e a singolo qubit rapido e ad alta fedeltà
examples.why: English pre-modifier stack kept in place, so the qualifiers "rapido e ad alta fedeltà" trail far from "controllo" and momentarily read as modifying "singolo qubit". Stiff rather than wrong.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no dropped caveats (the "gli utenti del piano Open non possono inviare job di Session" and the open-source **non** è / **sono** contrast both survive intact) — and the informal "tu" register is consistent (visita, esegui, Consulta, Esplora, installalo). The real defect is a glossary leak: "circuit" is left in English inside otherwise-Italian noun phrases, producing "l'esecuzione di Circuit quantistici" and "prendono Circuit astratti ... come input" where a native writer would write "circuiti quantistici" / "circuiti astratti"; note the file DOES translate every other domain noun (primitive, osservabili, carichi di lavoro), so the split is internal inconsistency, not a keep-in-English convention — the proper name "Circuit functions" is correctly kept. Secondary: "readout mitigation" becomes "la mitigazione della lettura" (should be "mitigazione degli errori di lettura"), "dynamical decoupling" becomes the hybrid "decoupling dinamico" instead of "disaccoppiamento dinamico", and "a variety of compute resource requirements" is amplified to "un'ampia varietà di requisiti". None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: ...from executing quantum circuits on quantum processors. / ...that take abstract circuits and desired measurement observables as input.
examples.suggested: ...dall'esecuzione di circuiti quantistici su processori quantistici. / ...che prendono circuiti astratti e osservabili di misura desiderati come input.
examples.translation: ...dall'esecuzione di Circuit quantistici su processori quantistici. / ...che prendono Circuit astratti e osservabili di misura desiderati come input.
examples.why: Untranslated English 'Circuit' capitalized mid-phrase inside an Italian noun phrase — a glossary leak, and inconsistent with the file's own practice of translating every other domain noun. Recognizable, so not misleading, but no Italian technical writer would leave it.

examples.source: Examples include dynamical decoupling for error suppression, and readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) for error mitigation.
examples.suggested: Alcuni esempi sono il disaccoppiamento dinamico per la soppressione degli errori, e la mitigazione degli errori di lettura e l'estrapolazione a rumore zero (ZNE) per la mitigazione degli errori.
examples.translation: Gli esempi includono il decoupling dinamico per la soppressione degli errori e la mitigazione della lettura e l'estrapolazione a rumore zero (ZNE) per la mitigazione degli errori.
examples.why: 'decoupling dinamico' is a half-calque (standard Italian is 'disaccoppiamento dinamico'), and 'mitigazione della lettura' literally says the readout itself is mitigated rather than its errors. The unpunctuated 'e ... e ...' chain also blurs which technique belongs to which category.

examples.source: Creating utility-scale quantum applications generally requires a variety of compute resource requirements.
examples.suggested: La creazione di applicazioni quantistiche su scala utility richiede generalmente requisiti di risorse di calcolo di vario tipo.
examples.translation: La creazione di applicazioni quantistiche su scala utility richiede generalmente un'ampia varietà di requisiti di risorse di calcolo.
examples.why: 'un'ampia varietà' strengthens the English 'a variety of' with an intensifier that is not in the source. Mild amplification only — it does not change what the reader can do.

examples.source: In addition to the open-source tools of the Qiskit SDK, Qiskit addons, and other tools...
examples.suggested: Oltre agli strumenti open-source di Qiskit SDK, degli addon Qiskit e di altri strumenti...
examples.translation: Oltre agli strumenti open-source di Qiskit SDK, dei componenti aggiuntivi Qiskit e di altri strumenti...
examples.why: 'Qiskit addons' is the product family name; rendering it as the generic 'componenti aggiuntivi Qiskit' over-translates a term the field keeps in English and breaks the reader's ability to search for it. Defensible but not the field convention.

examples.source: ...as well as easy resource management for multi-cloud and quantum-centric supercomputing use cases.
examples.suggested: ...nonché una gestione semplice delle risorse per casi d'uso multi-cloud e di supercalcolo quantum-centrico.
examples.translation: ...nonché una facile gestione delle risorse per casi d'uso multi-cloud e di supercalcolo centrato sul quantum.
examples.why: 'centrato sul quantum' mixes an Italian participle with a bare English noun and reads as translationese; the established Italian rendering is 'quantum-centrico'. Stiffness only, meaning intact.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the option/environment-variable descriptions (min_qpy_version の逆シリアル化, QISKIT_FORCE_THREADS の「シリアルに実行します」) track the English accurately, with トランスパイル / パスマネージャー / レイアウトおよびルーティングパス correct and consistent. Three editorial nits: (1) the Next-steps bullet uses the honorific「コントリビューションをご希望の方は」, a keigo slip against the plain desu/masu convention used everywhere else in the file; (2) QISKIT_PARALLEL renders generic "circuits" as「複数のCircuit」— capitalised bare English where a native writer would write「複数の回路」, and the file otherwise never uses 回路 at all, so the same concept appears as "Circuit drawer", "QuantumCircuit" and "Circuit" with no Japanese anchor; (3) QISKIT_SABRE_ALL_THREADS turns "greater than 20 CPUs/cores" into「20以上のCPU/コア」(≥20 rather than >20), a boundary shift in the threshold. None of these would mislead a learner about how the settings behave.

examples.source: Read the contributing guidelines if you want to contribute to the open-source Qiskit SDK.
examples.suggested: オープンソースのQiskit SDKに貢献したい場合は、[コントリビューションガイドライン](...)を読んでください。
examples.translation: オープンソースのQiskit SDKへのコントリビューションをご希望の方は、[コントリビューションガイドライン](...)を読んでください。
examples.why: 「ご希望の方は」is honorific customer-facing phrasing; the file's convention is plain desu/masu without keigo. Also sits oddly next to the plain「読んでください」in the same sentence.

examples.source: for example, transpilation over multiple circuits in Qiskit
examples.suggested: 例えば、Qiskitでの複数の回路のトランスパイルなどです。
examples.translation: 例えば、Qiskitで複数のCircuitに対するトランスパイルなどです。
examples.why: Generic "circuits" is left as capitalised bare English「Circuit」, which a Japanese technical writer would never do for a common noun (the API class name QuantumCircuit is a different case). The file therefore never gives the reader the ordinary term 回路.

examples.source: especially for systems with greater than 20 CPUs/cores
examples.suggested: 特に20を超えるCPU/コアを持つシステムで効果的ですが
examples.translation: 特に20以上のCPU/コアを持つシステムで効果的ですが
examples.why: 「20以上」means ≥20, whereas the English says strictly greater than 20 — a small boundary shift in the stated threshold. Consequence is low (a soft performance heuristic), but the number should match.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads a learner: the physics is faithful (변분 원리 → 측정된 에너지가 항상 진정한 바닥 상태 에너지의 상한, 힐베르트 공간 차원 $2^N$ 지수적 확장, SPSA가 반복당 두 번의 함수 호출로 전체 기울기 벡터를 근사), and core terms are correct and consistent (큐비트, 해밀토니안, 앤사츠, 기댓값, 최적화기, 프리미티브, 트랜스파일, 백엔드, 커플링 맵). The one real defect is within-file inconsistency on "circuit": Steps 2–3 leave it as bare English "Circuit" mid-sentence in Korean prose ("추상 Circuit", "Circuit 파라미터를 최적화하여", "최적화된 Circuit을 전달하고"), while the Background and later sections use the normal Korean 회로 ("Qiskit 회로 라이브러리", "대형 회로", "트랜스파일된 회로 깊이") — a native editor would unify on 회로. Secondary: the large-scale section softens the English "does not produce reliably reproducible results" into "재현 가능한 결과를 얻기 어렵습니다" (hard to obtain rather than does not reliably produce), and one SPSA sentence is calqued/stiff with stacked 의 particles ("노이즈로 인한 $f$의 정확한 값에서의 작은 편차"). Register holds: 해요체 imperatives throughout (확인하세요, 시도해 보세요), no 하십시오체 or 드리 forms.

examples.source: Input: Abstract circuit, observable / Since we optimized the circuit for the backend in Step 2 … / making optimization practically infeasible for large circuits
examples.suggested: Unify on 회로: "입력: 추상 회로, 관측 가능량", "2단계에서 백엔드에 맞게 회로를 최적화했으므로"
examples.translation: 입력: 추상 Circuit, 관측 가능량 / 2단계에서 백엔드에 맞게 Circuit을 최적화했으므로 … / 대형 회로에서의 최적화가 사실상 불가능해집니다
examples.why: "circuit" is rendered two ways inside one file — untranslated capitalized "Circuit" in Steps 2–3 prose, but 회로 in the Background, large-scale, and Challenge sections. 회로 is the settled Korean domain term; leaving bare English mid-sentence reads as a glossary leak, and the split makes the step I/O lists look like they name a distinct API object rather than the same concept discussed elsewhere.

examples.source: Combined with hardware noise, this means that scaling VQE to larger spin chains does not produce reliably reproducible results.
examples.suggested: 하드웨어 노이즈까지 겹치면, 더 큰 스핀 체인으로 VQE를 확장할 경우 안정적으로 재현 가능한 결과를 얻을 수 없습니다.
examples.translation: 하드웨어 노이즈와 결합되면, 더 큰 스핀 체인으로 VQE를 확장해도 재현 가능한 결과를 얻기 어렵습니다.
examples.why: The English is a flat statement that the results are not reliably reproducible; 얻기 어렵습니다 downgrades it to "it is difficult to obtain", which reads as a practical inconvenience rather than the stated limitation. The dropped "reliably" also removes the point that the failure is about reproducibility being unreliable, not merely hard-won.

examples.source: it is expected that small deviations in the exact values of $f$ coming from noise can be tolerated and accounted for
examples.suggested: 노이즈 때문에 $f$의 참값에서 생기는 작은 편차를 어느 정도 견디고 보정할 수 있으리라 기대할 수 있습니다
examples.translation: 노이즈로 인한 $f$의 정확한 값에서의 작은 편차를 허용하고 보정할 수 있습니다
examples.why: "$f$의 정확한 값에서의 작은 편차" stacks three 의/에서의 modifiers in English word order — grammatical but stiff, and a Korean technical writer would not chain them this way. The hedge "it is expected that" is also flattened into a flat assertion, losing the tentative framing of the intuition paragraph.

editor_note: No semantic inversions, hallucinations or dropped caveats — every Overview/Description paragraph tracks the English faithfully (screening step, pre-diagonalization, convergence check, the 20-qubit licence cap are all correct), so nothing here would teach a learner something false. The file's worst defect is byte-level: three UTF-8 replacement-character corruptions leave garbled words on the rendered page — line 64 "양자 화학 시���레이션" (시뮬레이션), line 256 "중요한 역���을" (역할을) and "활용��여" (활용하여); these need a repair pass. Terminology is otherwise sound but "qubit" is split three ways within the file — "Qubit" (lines 71, 160, 203), "큐비트" (line 92) and untranslated "qubit" in the headings/prose (lines 204, 249, 251, 254) — and "molecular geometry" is rendered throughout as 분자 기하학 (the mathematical discipline) where a Korean chemist writes 분자 구조 / 기하 구조. A few calqued constructions remain (the em-dash appositive in line 54, the "…라이선스를 취득하지 않는 한 그러합니다" tail in line 92, the doubled "~와 함께 … ~와 함께" in line 206), and line 98 drops the English "to your local environment"; register is consistent 합니다체 + ~하세요 with no 하십시오/드리 honorifics.

examples.source: so that users have greater computational control and improved accuracy in quantum chemistry simulations / plays crucial roles in various physiological processes
examples.suggested: 양자 화학 시뮬레이션 / 중요한 역할을 하는 / 활용하여
examples.translation: 사용자가 양자 화학 시���레이션에서 … / 다양한 생리적 과정에서 중요한 역���을 하는 … / homo-lumo 활성 오비탈 선택을 활용��여
examples.why: Three UTF-8 replacement-character (U+FFFD) corruptions destroy characters mid-word; the words render as black diamonds on the page. Context still carries the sense, so it is not misleading, but it is a genuine data-integrity defect that must be repaired.

examples.source: qubits
examples.suggested: 큐비트 throughout (e.g. "24큐비트 케이스", "40큐비트 N2 분자의 해리 PES 곡선")
examples.translation: "Qubit" (71, 160, 203) vs "큐비트" (92) vs untranslated "qubit" (204, 249, 251, 254)
examples.why: The core domain term is rendered three different ways inside one short file; 큐비트 is the established Korean convention and is already used once at line 92, so the other two forms are inconsistent rather than wrong.

examples.source: molecular geometry / the following geometries / six different geometries / differently separated geometries
examples.suggested: 분자 구조(기하 구조) / 다음 구조 및 옵션 / 6가지 서로 다른 분자 구조 / 서로 다른 원자간 거리의 구조
examples.translation: 분자 기하학 / 다음 기하학 및 옵션 / 6개의 서로 다른 기하학 / 서로 다른 분리 기하학
examples.why: 기하학 names the branch of mathematics; for a set of Cartesian coordinates a Korean chemist writes 분자 구조 or 기하 구조. Recognizable in context, so imperfect rather than false.

examples.source: use of this Qiskit Function is limited to problems requiring at most 20 qubits, unless a license is obtained granting a higher limit.
